commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Add keyframe-aware sampling to PyNvVideoCodec backend
commits.pr_body:
# [MM] Add keyframe-aware video sampling to PyNvVideoCodec ## Overview Uniform video sampling picks frame positions without regard to the stream's GOP structure, so reaching most sampled frames means decoding the intermediate frames back to the previous keyframe. On long videos, that decode work is significant. The primary win of this change is a 34% reduction in video decode time across all 900 VideoMME videos, and 56% on long videos. This PR adds a `keyframe_sampling="nearest"` option to the PyNvVideoCodec video backend. It moves the frame positions chosen by the existing loader to nearby keyframes, which decode without walking their GOP: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \ --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"backend": "pynvvideocodec", "keyframe_sampling": "nearest"}}' ``` ## Claims - **Decode time, VideoMME:** −34% across all 900 videos; −36% on N150, and −56% on its long videos. - **Serving, VideoMME N150 at 8 concurrent requests:** mean TTFT −60%, API-server CPU time per request −49%, request rate +58%. - **Accuracy is unchanged:** VideoMME N150 +0.23 pp [−2.13, +2.70]; Perception Test −0.31 pp [−1.04, +0.43]. - **Same frame count:** every video gets the requested number of frames. A video with fewer keyframes than samples keeps its uniform frames. - **Off by default:** with the option unset, nothing changes. Other video backends reject the option. ## Validation Unit tests, in `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` (PyNvVideoCodec 2.0.4): ```bash python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py ``` The new tests check that: - Selected keyframes are distinct and chronological, and ties go to the earlier keyframe. - Videos with too few usable keyframes fall back to their uniform frames. - The option reaches the PyNvVideoCodec backend, and invalid values and other backends reject it. - On CUDA, a real H.264 clip decodes the expected frames, which are checked by pixel content and by the returned `frames_indices`. ### Accuracy (Δ = nearest − uniform, pp, 95% CI) | Check | N | Δ pp | | --- | --- | --- | | VideoMME N150, reasoning on | 150 questions; 20 + 20 runs | +0.23 [−2.13, +2.70] | | Perception Test, reasoning on | 2,000 questions; 7 + 4 runs | −0.31 [−1.04, +0.43] | - **How the CIs are computed:** bootstrap paired by question. - **VideoMME mean accuracy:** 69.47% → 69.70%. - **Perception Test exercises the fallback:** clips request a median of 44 frames but contain only 3 keyframes, so all 552 clips keep their uniform frames. ### Decode time (nearest / uniform, geometric mean) | Workload | Ratio | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | | VideoMME, all 900 videos | 0.66× | **−34%** | | VideoMME N150 | 0.64× | **−36%** | | VideoMME N150, long videos | 0.44× | **−56%** | | Perception Test, 552 clips | 1.00× | unchanged | On VideoMME N150, about 56% of clips use keyframe sampling. The remaining 44%, mostly short videos, have too few keyframes and keep their original uniform samples. ### Serving, c=8 (VideoMME N150, mean over 20 runs per mode) | Metric | Uniform | Nearest | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Mean TTFT | 28.8 s | 11.5 s | **−60%** | | API-server CPU time per request | 17.9 CPU-s | 9.1 CPU-s | **−49%** | | Requests/s during the active window | 0.189 | 0.298 | **+58%** |
Setup, reproduction and more results **Setup** - **Model and hardware:** Nemotron 3 Nano Omni NVFP4, one B200 per server. - **Video:** PyNvVideoCodec decode, 2 FPS, ≤128 frames, `--video-pruning-rate 0.5`. - **Sampling:** reasoning on, T 0.6, top_p 0.95, `max_completion_tokens` 20480, `thinking_token_budget` 16384. - **VideoMME:** decode time measured offline through `VideoMediaIO` on all 900 videos. Accuracy and serving use N150 (150 questions across 145 clips), 20 runs per mode. - **Perception Test:** 2,000 questions across 552 clips. 3 decode repetitions per mode; 7 uniform and 4 nearest accuracy runs. - **Serving metrics:** per-run counter deltas and process telemetry sampled every 5 s, collected during the accuracy runs. - **Build:** upstream `dc45a5f` plus an earlier revision of this patch (`083d0abc`), whose `nearest` selection is identical to this PR's. **Reproduce** ```bash vllm serve --trust-remote-code --video-pruning-rate 0.5 \ --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 2, "num_frames": 128, "backend": "pynvvideocodec", "keyframe_sampling": "nearest"}}' ``` Omit `keyframe_sampling` for the uniform baseline.
## Details ### Design - **Targets:** the existing video loader still chooses the uniform frame positions. - **Keyframes:** read from PyNvVideoCodec's scanned stream metadata (`get_scanned_stream_metadata()`), only when the option is set. - **Selection:** a DP assigns one strictly increasing keyframe per target, minimizing total squared distance, so no keyframe is used twice and frames stay in order. Ties go to the earlier keyframe. Cost is O(targets × keyframes). - **Fallback:** a video with fewer usable keyframes than targets keeps its uniform positions. - **Metadata:** `frames_indices` reports the frames actually decoded, so models that derive timestamps from it see the correct timing. - **Decode:** the selected frames go through the existing decode path unchanged. ### Trade-offs and limitations - **Frames move in time:** sampled frames shift toward GOP boundaries, so their spacing is no longer even. Evaluate accuracy on the intended workload. - **Full-stream scan:** finding keyframes scans the whole stream, including for videos that then fall back. The decode times above include it. - **Workload-dependent:** the gain depends on keyframe density and the sampling budget. - **Scope:** PyNvVideoCodec only. Changes are limited to `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/`. - **Default:** off. **Related work:** #45203 proposed keyframe-only sampling through a separate PyAV loader, with duplication when keyframes were sparse. TorchCodec’s `seek_mode="approximate"` addresses a different cost: it skips the initial indexing scan while still attempting to retrieve the requested frames. This PR deliberately changes the sampling targets to nearby, distinct keyframes to reduce intermediate frame decode work. It extends the existing PyNvVideoCodec backend, preserves the model’s frame budget, and falls back to the original samples when too few keyframes are available. **AI assistance:** Claude Code and Codex were used for the implementation, review, figures and this description. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

## Overview

B300 presets for the single-node vLLM AgentX lane of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4871](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4871) (`vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k31-mc@sha256:f8199876…`).

| Preset | Concurrency | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `b300_agentx` | 1, 6 | TP8 + DCP8, low-latency decode, DSpark 4 tokens on TOKENSPEED_MLA |
| `b300_agentx_mixed_graphs` | 12, 24 | TP8 + DCP8, CUDA graphs for prefill and mixed steps up to 4096 tokens, DSpark 3 tokens |
| `b300_agentx_ep` | 48, 64, 72 | TP8 + DCP8 + EP8 MegaMoE, low-latency decode on FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1 at TP8
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#63893 gives every layer's K1 at TP4 the tuned paths of #63027's TP2 ratio-2 builds. That covers the attention seam and front, the DSpark draft's K1 included. The gate is `MonoBuild.tuned_front`:

```python
self.tuned or (not GFX942 and not self.generic and self.tp == 4)
```

With #64101 on main (`f97a8d6647`) admitting TP8, the same K1 paths compile at TP8 with no TP-specific change (CPU compile below). This PR widens the gate to `self.tp in (4, 8)`. The numerics test asserts that the target layers' K1 at TP8 is bit-exact against the generic build; it passes on 8x MI355X (below). Everything else stays as it is:
- gfx950 only;
- K2 stays generic;
- gfx942 still builds TP4 only;
- `generic=True` is still the bit-for-bit reference.

The one code change is the gate in `mono/layer.py`. The rest of the diff is the README line.

The test needs no new case. `_check_layers` already selects its tuned-vs-generic comparison by `runner.build_key(M, ratio).tuned_front`, and main (#64101) parametrizes `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm` with `tp in [2, 4, 8]`. With this gate, the TP8 case runs its ratio 0, 1 and 2 steps against a `generic=True` runner and asserts that they are equal bit for bit, as at TP4. Main's `mi355_8` CI step runs that case (`test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]`) and the TP8 layer cases `[8-8]` and `[8-28]` for any change under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`.

### Stacking (review only the last commit)

Fork branch `okorzh-amd/vllm:okorzh/dsv41-mono-tp8-tuned-k1`, head `0cc5f92bd5`, on main `4b47db922b`:

| Commit | From | Must land first |
|---|---|---|
| `96fa04ad7a`, `043dd8da90`, `37372f010c` | #63027 (tuned TP2 ratio-2 builds), rebased onto main | yes |
| `3d923a6848` | #63893 (tuned K1 at TP4) | yes |
| **`0cc5f92bd5`** | **this PR** | |

- **#64101 is on main as `f97a8d6647`.** Its cherry-pick `37598d94db` is gone, and with it the hand-resolved `back.py` `stage_split` conflict. This PR's commit is the old `d23e143e11` (`git range-diff`: identical) without the docstring and test-comment edits, because #63893's `3d923a6848` trimmed what they edited.
- **The rebase had one conflict,** in #63027's `stages/moe.py` `stage_route`, against main's #63816. As in #63893, it keeps #63816's NaN guard and `cursor < ept` mask, plus #63027's preloaded tuned bias.
- **The old resolution's `hh < d.heads` guard** on #63027's tuned whole-sector store in `stage_split` now belongs to #63027's rebase. `37372f010c` has the tuned branch without it. No build reaches that branch, this PR's included:
  - K2's `c["tuned"]` is `BackBuild.tuned` = `MonoBuild.tuned`, which is TP2 ratio 2 only, where `heads == heads_pad == 32`.
  - This PR widens only `tuned_front`.
  - Re-applying the guard leaves every K2 that can be built byte-identical (CPU compile below).

**Not included:** the "one poll batch for the tuned seam at TP8" fix. It changed `attn_words()` in `stages/seam.py` of #63027 @ `be9f259d42`, and that function is gone from #63027's current head (`d104a70f8d`; `37372f010c` here). At TP8 the tuned seam's TP poll is not built:
- K1's fused fold+slice reads the pend row (`reduce=False`).
- K2 stays generic. Its reduce polls 8 pairs in one batch under `POLL_MAX = 12`.

## Test Plan

1. CPU-only FlyDSL compile for gfx950 and gfx942: nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d56` with main's mono files, FlyDSL 0.4.0, amd-aiter 0.1.26, no devices.
   - **Trees:** this branch, its base (main + #63027 + #63893) and main `4b47db922b`, with the mono package of each tree mounted over the image's copy.
   - **Pushed vs compiled commits:** the full set was compiled from the local rebase `dbb2a0a03a` and its base `d3c0222f03`. They differ from `0cc5f92bd5` and `3d923a6848` only in comments and docstrings. Six configs rebuilt from each pushed commit are byte-identical.

   93 gfx950 builds per tree:
   - **TP8 K1:**
     - ratio 0, 1 and 2 at M = 1, 7, 14, 28, 48;
     - the fold=0 variant at M = 1, 48;
     - the index-source variant (ratio 1, 2) at M = 1, 7, 14, 28, 48;
     - the DSpark draft K1 (128 experts, top-3, one ug group, SWA 192) at M = 1, 7, 14, 28, 48.
   - **TP8 K2 and FFN:** K2 at ratio 0, 1 and 2 (M = 7, 48), the K2 index variant, the draft K2, and the FFN.
   - **TP2 and TP4:** K1 and K2 at ratio 0, 1 and 2 (M = 1, 7, 48), plus the index, fold=0, draft and FFN builds.

   Further sets:
   - **`generic=True`:** 8 builds across TP2, TP4 and TP8, on this branch and its base (main has no `generic`).
   - **gfx942:** 41 TP4/TP2 builds per tree.
   - **The guard:** 11 K2 builds with the old `hh < d.heads` guard re-applied: the TP2 tuned ratio-2 K2 at M = 7, 28, 48, plus all 8 TP8 K2 builds. Also 3 controls with `BackBuild.tuned` forced on at TP8.
   - Binaries are compared by the SHA-256 of the `gpu.binary` section, computed inside the image.
2. GPU, 8x MI355X:
   ```
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py -k "test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm and 8"
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k "8-8 or 8-28"
   ```
   Then the TP4 and TP2 cases, the step A/B of a TP8 `--monokernel` server against the base branch at conc 1, 2 and 4, and GSM8K.

## Test Result

**CPU compile:** every build compiles on every tree, except one pre-existing gfx942 failure:
- all 93 gfx950 builds and all 8 `generic=True` builds;
- every gfx942 build except the TP4 K2 at 48 rows. That build fails on main too: gfx942 caps decode at 42 rows (`MAX_ROWS_GFX942`), so the runner never builds it.

Every TP8 and TP4 build has 0 VGPR spills and 0 private segment. The one exception is pre-existing and byte-identical on both trees: #63027's tuned TP2 ratio-2 K2 at M=48 (256 VGPRs, 6 spilled, 28 B private segment; main: 253, no spill).

| TP8 K1 (ratio 0/1/2 alike) | M=1 | M=7 | M=14 | M=28 | M=48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VGPR, generic (base) | 122 | 142 | 142 | 167 | 239 |
| VGPR, tuned (this PR) | 132 | 148 | 148 | 148 | 154 |
| LDS (B), generic (base) | 29,184 | 38,944 | 69,632 | 78,400 | 78,400 |
| LDS (B), tuned (this PR) | 29,184 | 38,944 | 69,632 | 78,400 | 86,016 |

- **Variants:**
  - **Index source:** 134 VGPRs at M=1, and otherwise it matches the table. The generic build (base) uses 124 at M=1, 168 at M=28 and 240 at M=48. At M=28 and M=48 the tuned build also drops the generic build's lane spills (3 and 2 `v_writelane` -> 0).
  - **Draft K1:** matches the table.
  - **fold=0:** 132 VGPRs at M=1 (generic: 124) and 154 at M=48 (generic: 142).
- **LDS at M=48:** every M=48 variant of the tuned build uses 86,016 B, below TP4's tuned 86,592 B.
- **K2 at TP8:** VGPR and LDS are unchanged: 250 / 96,640 at M=7, 240 / 142,368 at M=48, and 199 for the draft K2.
  - Its binary changes because K1 and K2 of a width share one scratch layout, and K1's regions now take the tuned layout.
  - With immediates masked, the instruction stream is identical in all 8 builds.
  - The only differing instructions are 26 `s_add_u32` (27 in the index K2). Each one adds a region's base offset, and that offset moves by the growth of K1's tuned regions: +4,608 B at M=7 and +8,960 B at M=48.
  - TP4 has the same effect under #63893.
- **Byte-identical to the base:**
  - every TP2 build (24/24) and every TP4 build (24/24);
  - the TP8 FFN;
  - every `generic=True` build (8/8, including 6 at TP8), each also byte-identical to main's default build of the same config;
  - every gfx942 build that compiles (38/38).
- **The base is generic at TP8:** all 45 TP8 builds of the base are byte-identical to main.
- **The dropped guard is dead code:**
  - Re-applying it leaves all 11 K2 builds byte-identical.
  - Forcing K2's tuned path at TP8 changes the binary (3/3), but no `MonoBuild` produces that build.

**GPU (2026-10-30, 8x MI355X).** Images built from the pushed commits:
- **base:** nightly `3966924d56` + main `4b47db922b`'s mono files + #63027 + #63893 (`3d923a6848`). TP8 K1 is generic.
- **this PR:** base + `0cc5f92bd5`.

**Unit:**
- `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]`: PASS. The TP8 ratio 0, 1 and 2 steps of tuned K1 (M = 6, 7, 12, 36, 48) equal the `generic=True` build bit for bit, then 300 CUDA-graph replays.
- **Controls:**
  - On the base it passes too, but there the compare is vacuous, because TP8 K1 is generic.
  - This branch plus a one-ulp mutation that only TP8 tuned K1 compiles FAILS at `ratio 1, 1 x 6`. So the compare is live.
- `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]` and `[8-28]`: PASS.
- Non-regression on this branch: `[4]`, `[2]`, `[4-8]` and `[2-8]` PASS.

**Step A/B:**
- **Server:** one TP8 `--monokernel` server per session, on the CI C1 recipe at tp=8: aiter MoE, no EP, DSpark k=6, adaptive verification off, Engram host offload off.
- **Load:** `vllm bench serve` random 32k in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic acceptance length 3.87. The step is ITL p50.
- **Design:** ABBA over 4 rounds (3 x 32 prompts per conc, round and arm).
- **GSM8K:** 1319 questions, greedy, real (block-rejection) acceptance, at `--parallel 6` so that every step stays on the mono kernels. 4 base passes and 2 passes on this PR.

| TP8 mono | conc 1 step | conc 2 step | conc 4 step | GSM8K / AL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (generic K1) | 5.129 ms | 6.015 ms | 7.845 ms | 0.920 / 3.580 |
| this PR (tuned K1) | 4.875 ms | 5.753 ms | 7.660 ms | 0.921 / 3.569 |
| delta | **-254 us (-4.9%)** | **-262 us (-4.4%)** | **-185 us (-2.4%)** | +0.0015 / -0.011 |

- **Every round is faster:** this PR wins in 4 of 4 paired rounds at each conc. The round deltas are -242..-268 us (conc 1), -238..-282 us (conc 2) and -165..-206 us (conc 4).
- **Noise:** the A/A spread of the per-round means is at most 34 us.
- **The saving is K1's.** Per decode step, from the torch profiler (8-rank mean), K1's GPU time drops by:
  - 250 us at 7 target rows (target 234, draft 16);
  - 261 us at 14 rows (target 244, draft 17).
- **GSM8K:** the difference is +0.0015. The standard error of a difference of two n=1319 passes is ~0.0105.
- **Greedy identity probe** (256 GSM8K prompts, `--parallel 1`): it cannot test bit-exactness on this setup.
  - Two base servers produce token-identical answers on only 70-81 of 256 prompts; base vs this PR on 67-72.
  - Each run, base or this PR, has 5-10 answers that differ from every other run. This PR has 5, all with the same final answer.

For scale: on 10-27, an older stack (#63027 @ `be9f259d42`) with tuned K1, X8R at TP8 and a poll-batch fix enabled together took -261 us at conc 1. Tuned K1 alone now takes -254 us.

**Not bit-compared on GPU:**
- the DSpark draft's TP8 K1: its only check is acceptance, and AL moves by -0.011;
- the fold=0 and index-source K1, which the layers test checks only to a tolerance;
- the conc 2 / 4 widths, 14 and 28 rows (the numerics test runs M = 6, 7, 12, 36, 48).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
commits.pr_body:
This carries #56831 by @CedricHwong forward to current main. That PR has been idle since 09-14 and no longer passes CI after the rebase. Cedric's commit is kept unchanged, with his authorship. The two commits on top address the review comments on that PR.

Adaptive verification (DSpark) picks the per-step draft budget on the host from rank-local stale confidences, then picks which slots to keep on the device from rank-local live confidences. If TP ranks disagree on either one, they run different batch layouts: different token counts, or equal totals with different request boundaries. That breaks the collectives that follow and can hang them (#54011). This PR makes TP rank 0 authoritative:

1. `get_num_tokens`: `draft_budget` is broadcast with `broadcast_object` (shm MessageQueue, host only).
2. `reallocate_drafts`: on steps that trim, the per-request `capacities` are broadcast from rank 0 before `cu_num_logits` / `query_start_loc` are built.

Both conditions around (2), `draft_budget == 0` and `draft_budget < scheduled drafts`, depend only on the broadcast budget and scheduler-provided counts. Every TP rank therefore takes the same branch, and the collective cannot be entered unevenly.

### Changes vs #56831

- **Test updates for current main.** #56888 renamed `async_copy_to_gpu` to `async_tensor_h2d`; the old monkeypatch no longer resolved, giving 12 failures, and `cpu.yaml` runs `-x`. #58466 made `reallocate_drafts` also return the admitted draft counts. #63421 replaced the compiled budget assignment with a Triton kernel; the CPU test stands in for it with its global top-k reference. #55939 made `tests/v1/spec_decode` type-checked, so the test now narrows `_batch_budget` before indexing it.
- **Real multi-rank test.** `test_tp_ranks_agree_on_verification_layout[2, 4]` spawns gloo ranks with a real TP `GroupCoordinator` and drives the real `get_num_tokens` / `reallocate_drafts`. The ranks' confidences differ by one fp32 ULP, across three cases: a draft-budget tie, an equal-total boundary split, and 64 randomized steps. Every rank must end up with the leader's budget, capacities, `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc`. It replaces the single-process budget emulation.
- **Transport.** The capacities sync uses plain `get_tp_group().broadcast`, i.e. c10d on the TP device group, as in #56831.
  - Routing `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` through the device communicator (PyNCCL) would be about 2x cheaper per call. On CUDA it would also avoid creating the device group's NCCL communicator on the first trimmed step. But it changes every `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` caller (PCP `sync_drafts` too) and needs XPU validation, so it will be a separate PR.

Scope: this covers TP. It also covers DCP when PCP = 1; DCP groups span PCP before TP. With PCP > 1, each PCP slice's TP group has its own leader. Since #61994, DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA rejects AV + PCP (it requires fixed-length DSpark). The generic `PCPManager` path still admits it, which predates this PR and is a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, plus `mypy` / `ruff` via the pre-commit pins.
- Multi-rank CPU harness: real gloo groups, the real `GroupCoordinator` and the real `AdaptiveVerificationManager`. TP 2/4/8, with injected per-rank confidence drift from 1 ULP to large.
- MI355X microbenchmark of both collectives, using vLLM's real TP group (`init_distributed_environment` + `initialize_model_parallel`) at TP2/TP4.
- MI355X end to end:
  - Model: Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` with `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, V2 model runner, ROCM_ATTN.
  - Workload: 600 GSM8K CoT prompts, output 512, greedy.
  - A/B: main vs this PR, conc 1/16/64, 4 interleaved rounds per arm.
  - Divergence check: an instrumented main that all-gathers every rank's locally computed budget, capacities and confidences on every step.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests** (on main `7e3e3f6ab6`): `test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 31 passed and 7 skipped (the CUDA-only kernel tests). mypy and ruff are clean, and the real-rank test passed 10 of 10 runs.
  - **Without the budget broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the budget tie; 36/64 random steps diverge at TP2, 53/64 at TP4.
  - **Without the capacities broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the boundary case (4/64 random steps at TP2, 10/64 at TP4: equal totals, different request boundaries). The emulated reallocation tests at TP 2/4/8 fail too.
- **Multi-rank harness:** 0 mismatches on this branch at every world size and drift level.
  - Without the fix, a single fp32 ULP is enough to change the layout. Mismatching steps per 1000 at TP 2/4/8 (capacities or boundaries):
    - 1-16 ULP: 0-2
    - 1e-4 relative: 2-9
    - 1e-2 relative: 65-382
  - Most mismatches have equal totals across ranks but different request boundaries.
- **Per-step cost, MI355X, p50 (p90), slowest rank:**

| | TP2 | TP4 |
|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_object(budget)`: every step that has drafts, host only | 6.7 us (7.5) | 7.9 us (8.2) |
| `capacities` broadcast (c10d, as in this PR): trimmed steps only. Host enqueue + in-stream GPU time; does not depend on num_reqs from 1 to 256 | ~32 + ~25 us | ~33 + ~26 us |
| Worst-case total for a trimmed step, with no overlap | ~64 us | ~68 us (p90 ~76) |

  That is 0.4-1.4% of a 5-15 ms decode step, at most. The host part overlaps GPU work under async scheduling. With PyNCCL (the planned follow-up), a trimmed step costs about 25-29 us.
- **End to end at TP2, measured with the capacities sync on PyNCCL (an earlier revision of this PR); the c10d path still needs an e2e run (GPUs were busy): no measurable regression.** Each delta is within about 1.2 standard deviations; run-to-run CV is 0.2-0.6%.

| conc | output tok/s, main | output tok/s, this PR | delta | TPOT p50, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 721.0 ± 4.1 | 727.7 ± 10 | +0.9% | 1.311 → 1.314 ms |
| 16 | 5489 ± 12 | 5493 ± 15 | +0.1% | 2.755 → 2.763 ms |
| 64 | 10590 ± 50 | 10585 ± 19 | -0.1% | 5.615 → 5.629 ms |

  Acceptance length is unchanged (±0.7%). There were 0 failed requests in 24 runs. The `capacities` broadcast fired on about 97% of c16/c64 steps and about 7% of c1 steps.
- **Natural divergence was not observed on this setup.**
  - Instrumented main ran 8434 steps at TP2 and 7886 steps at TP4: 0 budget, capacities or confidence mismatches.
  - A separate DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MI355X serving trace ran about 478k AV steps, also with 0 mismatches.
  - Here the confidence inputs are bitwise identical across ranks, because the custom all-reduce sums in a fixed rank order. Divergence needs rank-asymmetric numerics, such as rank-order-dependent reductions, non-deterministic kernels, or the TP8 H20 DeepSeek-V4 setup in #54011.
  - The fix is cheap insurance against that: per the numbers above, about 7 us host per step plus about 19 us per trimmed step.

Co-authored with @CedricHwong (original fix, #56831). Supersedes #56831.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Allow lut_b_moe online quantization on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `lut_b_moe` to `RocmPlatform.supported_quantization` so `quantization="lut_b_moe"` passes validation on ROCm and uses the LUT-B emulation experts, as the docs say it should for non-Rubin GPUs. This fixes `tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe` on ROCm. That test fails on ROCm and is one of the failures the ROCm Quantization re-enable in vllm#66672 currently works around.

Fixes #<issue-to-be-filed>. Culprit: vllm#62759.

## Claims

- `quantization="lut_b_moe"` no longer fails with `ValidationError: lut_b_moe quantization is currently not supported in rocm.` on ROCm. It loads, falls back to `LutBEmulationTritonExperts`, and generates coherent output.
- `test_online_lut_b_moe` passes on gfx950 with this change. It has never passed on ROCm since it was added.
- No behavior change on NVIDIA or XPU. `CudaPlatform` has no allow-list here, and the XPU list is not touched.

## Validation

All runs were on MI355X (gfx950), from `tests/`, with torchao off the default path in `/tmp/qdeps` (installed from vllm#66672's `requirements/test/quantization_deps_rocm.txt`).

| Check | Command | Before (`origin/main` b76e2401f8) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reproducer | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=<worktree>:/tmp/qdeps .venv/bin/python -m pytest quantization/test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe` | 1 failed (pydantic `ValidationError` from `ModelConfig`: `lut_b_moe quantization is currently not supported in rocm.`) | 1 passed (42s). The log shows `LUT-B MoE falls back to emulation: kernel does not support current device rocm`, and greedy output is `'Hello my name is' -> ' Mary. I'` |
| Neighbouring online methods | `pytest quantization/test_online.py -k 'lut_b or nvfp4_per_token_moe or mxfp4_hadamard'` | - | 1 passed, 1 skipped (`nvfp4_per_token_moe` is CUDA-only), 200 deselected |
| LUT-B kernels / config args | `pytest kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py` | - | 52 passed, 7 skipped (all 7 are SM107/Rubin native-kernel tests) |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/rocm.py` | - | clean |

The compiled extensions came from a slightly older main (5629b26146). That does not matter here because no csrc code is involved; this is a Python allow-list change only.

**Not covered locally:**
- gfx942 (MI300) was not run. I expect it to behave the same, because the allow-list check is not arch-gated and ROCm always takes the emulation experts. However, the emulation's activation QDQ goes through the ROCm Triton MXFP8 quantizer (`_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_triton`), which is only tested in-tree on gfx95x. The already allow-listed `mxfp8` online method has the same dependency. The MI300 Quantization job that vllm#66672 re-enables should confirm this.
- NVIDIA was not run. It is unaffected because the ROCm list is the only thing that changes.

CI: the existing `test_online_lut_b_moe` (gated on `is_cuda_alike()`) is the regression guard. It runs in the ROCm Quantization jobs once vllm#66672 re-enables them. No new test is needed.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Platform.verify_quantization` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) rejects any method that is missing from a platform's non-empty `supported_quantization` list. vllm#62759 (df05643664, "[Quant] LUT-B MoE with MXFP8 activations: native Rubin kernel + emulation") added the `lut_b_moe` shorthand to `QuantizationMethods` and `_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS`, along with the emulation experts and `test_online_lut_b_moe`. It did not add the shorthand to `RocmPlatform.supported_quantization`, where the other online shorthands (`mxfp8`, `fp8_per_*`, `mxfp4_hadamard32`) are listed. ROCm does not actually lack the feature. `LutBEmulationTritonExperts._supports_current_device` returns `is_cuda_alike()`, the native `LutBSm107Experts` requires `is_cuda()`, and `docs/features/quantization/online.md` says "Other GPUs emulate the same numerics". The method was simply rejected before it could be built. I found the culprit with `git log -S lut_b_moe`, which returns only that commit, so no bisect was needed. The test was added while the ROCm Quantization job was disabled (since 2026-10-25), so the failure went unnoticed.

**Fix.** One line: add `"lut_b_moe"` next to `mxfp4_hadamard32`. With this change, the only behavior difference is that ROCm accepts `quantization="lut_b_moe"` instead of rejecting it.

**Interaction with open PRs:**
- vllm#66672 (`Thangnguyenvn98`) and vllm#66803 (`fxmarty-amd`) both change the `test_online_lut_b_moe` gate from `is_cuda_alike()` to `is_cuda()` with "ROCm does not support lut_b_moe". That would skip the test on ROCm rather than fix it. With this PR, those hunks should be dropped and the `is_cuda_alike()` gate kept. Otherwise this fix loses its regression guard on ROCm. This PR unblocks that case in vllm#66672's re-enabled MI300/MI355 Quantization jobs.
- vllm#66607 (`mgoin`, LUT-B for linear layers) adds a `lut_b` shorthand and `test_online_lut_b`, also gated on `is_cuda_alike()`, without a ROCm allow-list entry. It will hit the same `ValidationError` on ROCm, so `lut_b` should be added to the ROCm list either in that PR or in a follow-up after it merges.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `lut_b_moe`, `LUT-B`, `lut_b rocm` and `supported_quantization rocm`. The hits were vllm#66607, #66803, #66672, #66874 (compressed-tensors LUT-B MoE checkpoints; does not touch platforms), #66194, #65802, #60321, #62770 and #65165. None of them adds `lut_b_moe` to the ROCm allow-list.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed the diff and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Keep the AttnRes block bank in a persistent workspace
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Kimi-K3 on ROCm allocates two ~1.8 GB buffers on every prefill step, each sized by the step's token count. The caching allocator keeps the slightly-too-small leftovers, so its cache grows while serving until something fails. What fails depends on how vLLM sizes the KV cache:
- **Extensible KV cache off** (the V1 model runner, which DBO uses, ROCm KV connectors such as MoRIIO/NIXL/Mooncake, or an explicit KV size): ROCr can't get scratch memory and aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. Every request fails.
- **Extensible KV cache on** (vllm#56492, the default with the V2 runner): torch's allocator is capped, so the leftovers turn into allocator OOM-and-retry cycles and a larger warmup reserve that costs KV cache. Under TP4 x PP2 the capped pool runs out and requests fail.

This PR fixes one of the two buffers: the AttnRes block bank in `KimiLinearModel` now comes from the workspace manager as one persistent buffer, sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, instead of a fresh allocation per forward. The other buffer is AITER's MoE stage-2 target, fixed by ROCm/aiter#7363. Both are needed, and on current vLLM they have to land together (see [Merge order](#merge-order)). SGLang has the same bank and fixes it in sgl-project/sglang#48164.

## Claims

- With ROCm/aiter#7363, Kimi-K3 serves in the configurations where stock fails: extensible KV cache off (stock fails every request) and TP4 x PP2 (stock fails the 1k conc 64 and 128 benchmarks).
- On the default TP8 path, 2 allocator retries instead of 10 over the benchmark sequence, a 1.61 GiB warmup transient reserve instead of 4.92 GiB, and 2.2% more KV cache tokens.
- No accuracy change and no throughput regression (8k in: 1254.6 ± 18.5 vs 1261.9 ± 19.4 tok/s over 4 samples per arm).
- Must reach vLLM in the same build as ROCm/aiter#7363 (AITER v0.1.29): merge right after the separate AITER pin bump; either one alone fails on current vLLM (see [Merge order](#merge-order)).

## Validation

**Setup** (8x MI355X): `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly pinned by digest (`sha256:5800b3b4...`), vLLM `40941f2c4`, AITER 0.1.27, with this branch and ROCm/aiter#7363 applied ("fixed") or neither ("stock"). Server env and args as the perf-eval `kimi_k3-mi355x` workload: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code`. Benchmarks: the workload's `vllm bench serve` sequence (random, `--ignore-eos`): 8k/1k conc 128 n 512, then 1k/1k at conc 1/64/128. Memory sampled every 2 s on every rank.

**Default path (extensible KV cache on, TP8)**: both complete every benchmark.

| phase | stock: free cached segments | stock: allocator retries | fixed: free cached segments | fixed: allocator retries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k in, conc 128 | 7.9 GiB | 6 | 2.9 GiB | 1 |
| 1k in, conc 1 | 7.8 GiB | 6 | 2.5 GiB | 1 |
| 1k in, conc 64 | 8.1 GiB | 8 | 2.4 GiB | 2 |
| 1k in, conc 128 | 8.0 GiB | 10 | 2.3 GiB | 2 |

"Free cached segments": segments the caching allocator holds with no live block (max over ranks). "Allocator retries": torch's cumulative OOM-free-cache-retry count (max over ranks). Free device memory is near zero by design on this path, since the KV cache is extended into it after warmup. Stock's per-step allocations also inflate the transient reserve that warmup measures (4.92 vs 1.61 GiB), so it ends up with less KV cache: 2,754,513 vs 2,816,284 tokens (3612–3669 vs 3693–3752 blocks per rank).

**Extensible KV cache off** (`--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`, the sizing used by the V1 runner, ROCm KV connectors and explicit KV sizes): stock fails every request from the first benchmark (0/512 at 8k in), aborting with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` at 0.00 GiB free. Fixed completes everything with free cached segments at 2.7–3.4 GiB, at least 7.6 GiB free, no allocator retries, and gsm8k 0.9629 ± 0.0052.

**TP4 x PP2**: stock completes 8k in and 1k conc 1, then fails 128/256 requests at 1k conc 64 and all 512 at 1k conc 128: `torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 182.00 MiB ... 13.14 GiB is free. 196.91 GiB allowed`, after 300–312 allocator retries. Fixed completes everything, gsm8k on 250 questions 0.984 ± 0.008, with 16–35 allocator retries on the last-stage GPUs (see the open item under [Merge order](#merge-order)).

- **gsm8k** (5-shot, perf-eval's lm_eval settings, TP8): 0.9651 ± 0.0051 stock vs 0.9621 ± 0.0053 fixed.
- **fp8 stage 2** (`AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`, as in the Kimi-K3 recipe): fixed completes everything, gsm8k 0.9636 ± 0.0052.
- **Unit tests** (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py`, CPU): `KimiLinearModel.forward` over consecutive steps of different sizes must return block residuals that are views of the same persistent workspace bank; plus per-micro-batch banks across the workspace lock, the size bound, and the no-workspace fallback. On this image: 6/6 fail on stock (per-step `new_empty`), 6/6 pass with this change.
- **Multimodal:** 16 image+text prompts at temperature 0; outputs vary between runs of the same version (5/16 identical stock vs fixed, 6/16 stock vs stock in an earlier run), so exact-match comparison doesn't separate the versions.
- **Speculative decoding (DSpark)**, measured on the Oct 26 image (vLLM `00b6c4c56`, AITER 0.1.26) with the previous revision `c4696ae1ae`, whose path without DBO is the same, and the earlier AITER fix ROCm/aiter#6965: TP8 with the speculative config from vLLM's Kimi-K3 DSpark CI eval and `--max-num-seqs 128`, gsm8k 0.9674 ± 0.0049 stock vs 0.9629 ± 0.0052 fixed, mean acceptance length 5.30–5.48 vs 5.34–5.40.
- **End-to-end not in CI:** reproducing needs 8x MI355X with the Kimi-K3 weights, which vLLM CI doesn't have, so the runs above were manual.

**Throughput** (TP8 default path, nothing else on the GPUs, 4 servers stock/fixed/stock/fixed with 2 repeats each, so 4 samples per arm):

| bench | out tok/s (stock / fixed) | mean TPOT | median TPOT | TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k in, conc 128 | 1254.6 ± 18.5 / 1261.9 ± 19.4 (+0.6%) | 91.44 / 90.90 ms | 97.38 / 97.01 ms | 10701 / 10641 ms |
| 1k in, conc 1 | 71.29 ± 0.94 / 72.80 ± 0.57 (+2.1%) | 13.80 / 13.50 ms | 13.80 / 13.50 ms | 252 / 255 ms |

## Details

**Root cause.** Two per-step buffers are each num_tokens x 114,688 B, about 1.8 GB for a 16k-token chunk at TP8:
- this model's AttnRes bank, `[num_tokens, num_blocks, hidden]` bf16;
- AITER's FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce target, `[num_tokens, topk, model_dim]` bf16.

The caching allocator never serves a request from a smaller free segment and never merges segments, so every step slightly larger than the last allocates new ~1.8 GB segments and keeps the old ones. On the Oct 26 image, a snapshot just before the crash had 14.5 GiB in fully free segments; seven were 1766–1772 MiB, just under the failing 1774 MiB request, and their recorded stacks point at exactly these two call sites. Torch recovers its own allocations by emptying the cache and retrying. ROCr cannot, so with the extensible KV cache off the next scratch acquisition fails; with it on, torch's cap holds the cache back, at the cost of the retries and reserve above.

**Change.** `_new_block_residual` takes a `(max_num_batched_tokens, num_blocks, hidden)` buffer from `current_workspace_manager().get_persistent()` and slices it per step. The profiling run allocates it before the workspace locks, so it is inside the measured peak. The runner sizes its own input buffers to `max_num_batched_tokens`, so no forward can need more rows; an assert guards it.
- **PP:** every rank uses the bank, including non-last ranks that send it. `gpu_worker.execute_model` waits for the previous step's sends before the next forward.
- **No workspace manager** (e.g. unit tests): falls back to the per-step allocation.
- **DBO:** the workspace manager keeps persistent buffers per micro-batch slot by design ([`get_persistent_resource`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e8570ef757b67805797b005b59fcd6600d939421/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py#L146): "Each ubatch/lane pair has a separate cache"), so each slot gets its own bank: one extra bank under DBO, 1.75 GiB at 16k tokens (0.44 GiB at the recipe's 4096). Both slots get their bank during warmup, before the workspace locks. Measured with DP2 x TP4 + EP + `--enable-dbo`, `--max-num-seqs 128` (the recipe's value): KV cache on rank 0 is 52.48 GiB stock vs 50.64 GiB with this PR, and startup completes with no workspace-lock error for the bank. End-to-end serving under DBO could not be measured for any version: on stock vLLM the first benchmark batch fails with `AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'modular_kernel.py:1207:_allocate_buffers' requires 213.50 MB, current size is 112.00 MB` (the MoE workspace isn't sized for the DP-gathered token count before the lock), and with the default `max_num_seqs` startup runs out of memory during graph capture. Both reproduce without this PR (#65106, #65105), on the Oct 26 image and on the Nov 4 nightly (vLLM `dd4e40142`).

### Why both PRs

On current vLLM with only this PR (stock AITER), every request fails: `torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 1.70 GiB ... 202.94 GiB allowed` at AITER's stage-2 target (`aiter/fused_moe.py:3178`, `_flydsl_v2_stage2_wrapper`). The persistent bank no longer inflates the transient reserve that warmup measures (3.17 GiB instead of stock's 4.92), and AITER's per-call 1.70 GiB target then doesn't fit under the allocator cap. With ROCm/aiter#7363 as well, everything completes (above). On the Oct 26 image, before the extensible KV cache, the same vLLM-only run finished but bottomed out at 0.12 GiB free with free cached segments still growing by 5 GiB.

### History

The nightly started crashing on Oct 3: a `git bisect` between builds 628 and 631 found #58344 (Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoints on ROCm), which makes the same two buffers fill the headroom within the first 8k benchmark. Since #57392 made the gluon prefill backend (checkpoints off) the default, the crash moved to the 1k conc 128 benchmark, and [build 249](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/249) survived the same code by luck. On that image, this change plus the earlier AITER fix ROCm/aiter#6965 also made the fused backend with checkpoints on complete everything (free cached flat at 6.0–6.3 GiB, gsm8k 0.9591 ± 0.0055); restoring from a checkpoint is untested.

### Merge order

This change and [ROCm/aiter#7363](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7363) have to reach vLLM in the same build. #7363 is merged in AITER (Nov 5) and is expected in v0.1.29; vLLM's current pin, v0.1.28.post1, was cut before it. The bump to v0.1.29 will come in a separate vLLM PR, and this PR should merge right after it, with no nightly in between, not before it and not on v0.1.28.post1. With the extensible KV cache (vllm#56492), vLLM reserves scratch space for the temporary memory it sees during warmup. On stock, both buffers (this model's bank and AITER's stage-2 target) are allocated every step, so warmup reserves room for both (4.92 GiB), and that room absorbs both sets of leftovers. Each fix makes one buffer persistent and shrinks the reserve, and the other buffer's per-step allocation then fails, failing almost every request:

| | warmup reserve | result |
|---|---|---|
| this PR only | 3.17 GiB | `OutOfMemoryError` allocating AITER's 1.70 GiB target (`aiter/fused_moe.py:3178`) |
| aiter#7363 only | 3.36 GiB | `OutOfMemoryError` allocating this model's 1.71 GiB bank (`linear.py:894`) |
| both | 1.61 GiB | everything completes |

Rounding AITER's target to a power of two instead (ROCm/aiter#6965) doesn't avoid this: with this PR it fails the same way (`Tried to allocate 1.75 GiB` at `fused_moe.py:3179`), since the target is still allocated every call. Measured with AITER 0.1.27; v0.1.28.post1 allocates the target the same way.

**Open (TP4 x PP2 only):** with both fixes, the last-stage GPUs still see transient spikes of up to 13 GiB of free cached segments while serving, which allocator retries release (16–35 retries vs 2–4 on the first stage); requests complete. The source isn't identified yet and is separate from the two buffers here.

### Revisions

- **`86ed9fb065`..`8bed270c99`** (initial): the bank comes from the workspace manager (`get_persistent`), sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, on every PP rank.
- **`c4696ae1ae`**: a model-owned bank shared by the DBO micro-batches at their token offsets, to avoid the extra bank under DBO.
- **`ebb611c61a`** (review): back to the workspace bank, identical to `8bed270c99`. One bank per micro-batch slot is the workspace manager's design, and the extra bank under DBO is acceptable. Adds the forward-level regression tests to `test_amd_attn_res.py` (replacing `test_amd_attn_res_bank.py`).
- **`f7a51de972`**: narrows `forward`'s return type in the test for mypy.

Validation above was re-run on vLLM `40941f2c4` (Nov 3, with the extensible KV cache) against ROCm/aiter#7363, except where marked as the Oct 26 image.

This PR was authored with assistance from Claude Code.

commits.pr_title: [Doc][Recipe] Muse Spark Open: DSpark + specialized decode mode; gate Kimi-K3.1 low-latency decode off AMD
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds a **DSpark + specialized decode** method to the Muse Spark Open recipe. It covers the GB300 specialized decode from #64077 (`--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'`) and the MI355X monokernel from #63440 (`--monokernel`). Before this PR, the recipe documented only the MI355X path, as a manual guide step, and the command builder could not emit either path.

Also gates Kimi-K3.1-Pro's `low_latency_decode` feature off AMD, where its command fails at startup.

## Claims

- On GB300 + NVFP4, selecting the method emits DSpark with `enable_adaptive_verification: false` plus `decode_backend=latency_specialized`. The specialized decode refuses adaptive verification, and the recipe's default DSpark config enables it.
- On MI355X + MXFP4, selecting the method emits the existing AMD DSpark profile plus `--monokernel`.
- The method is opt-in and gated to the variants and GPUs it runs on. Elsewhere it is not offered, and the builder keeps plain DSpark. Default commands do not change.
- Muse Spark Open: `default_variant` now names NVFP4 for NVIDIA. Before, switching the builder from an AMD GPU to NVIDIA fell back to BF16, the largest variant that fits, which leaves DSpark off and offers only one spec method. Switching back to AMD then kept BF16.
- Kimi-K3.1-Pro: `low_latency_decode` is no longer offered on AMD. On MI355X, `decode_backend=latency_specialized` selects the separate `kimi_k3/amd` path, which needs DSpark and `max_num_seqs × (K + 1) ≤ 16` and is written for Kimi-K3's shapes. Turning the feature on there produced a command that failed at startup.
- A note and the guide state that the pinned `muse-spark-open` images (pushed 2026-10-15) predate both implementations. Serving this method needs a nightly at or after `4fab5a0`, which contains #64077 and #63440.

## Validation

Recipe validator (the same check as this repo's `Recipes` PR check), run from a checkout of vllm-project/recipes:

```
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir ~/vllm/recipes
✓ vllm recipes from ~/vllm/recipes are valid against the renderer
```

Rendered commands, through the builder's `resolveSelection`:

| Selection | Result |
|---|---|
| gb300, NVFP4, TEP (default) | unchanged: DSpark with adaptive verification on |
| gb300, NVFP4, TEP, `fmode=spec_decoding:dspark_specialized` | `--speculative-config {…"enable_adaptive_verification":false} --additional-config {"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}` |
| mi355x, MXFP4, TEP, `dspark_specialized` | AMD DSpark profile + `--monokernel`, with the same AITER env |
| gb200, NVFP4, TEP, `dspark_specialized` | mode unavailable, falls back to plain DSpark |
| mi355x, BF16, `dspark_specialized` | mode unavailable, falls back to plain DSpark |
| Kimi-K3.1-Pro: gb300, `low_latency_decode` | unchanged |
| Kimi-K3.1-Pro: mi355x, `low_latency_decode` | feature unavailable, no `--additional-config` |

The emitted flags were checked against the startup checks in `vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` (`unsupported`) and `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/mono/decoder.py` (`deployment_refusals`, `layer_refusals`).

**Not yet validated on hardware:** the generated commands have not been served on GB300 or MI355X with the nightly image. This PR stays a draft until they are.

## Details

- **Why a `spec_decoding` mode, not a separate feature.** Both paths serve only DSpark verify steps. A separate feature cannot require `spec_decoding` to be on, and on NVIDIA it also cannot turn off adaptive verification in that feature's JSON: features emit in selection order and are deduped last-wins. A mode carries its own `--speculative-config`, and the schema gates modes by `variants` and `hardware`.
- **Scope.** NVIDIA is limited to GB300, the only GPU #64077 was measured on; the code also accepts other SM100/SM103 GPUs. MI355X is limited to the MXFP4 variant, because the monokernel requires Quark MXFP4 W4A4 experts.
- **Known limitation.** Modes cannot be gated by strategy or by the (variant, GPU) pair. The method can therefore still be selected with a non-TEP strategy, with multi-node TEP on MI355X (the monokernel needs TP8), or with NVFP4 on MI355X. In those cases vLLM refuses at startup with the reason. The method description and the guide state the requirements.
- **Other models considered.** A `spec_decoding` mode fits only where the specialized decode requires DSpark. Kimi-K3/K3.1 on NVIDIA, MiniMax-M3, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro/V4.1 on AMD (`--monokernel`) run without speculative decoding, so they belong in a standalone feature like K3.1-Pro's `low_latency_decode`; that is left for follow-ups. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300 needs DSpark but also exactly TP4, and the builder resolves single-node TP to TP2 on GB300. A mode cannot set TP, so it is left out; B300 keeps the `b300_agentx_tp` preset.
- **Overlap.** #64084 (draft, gfx942 MXFP4) edits other parts of the same recipe and may need a trivial rebase. #63527 (draft) would add fp8 KV to the MI355X path, so the guide's bf16 KV requirement should be updated when it lands.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds the specialized decode to this recipe; searched open PRs for "Muse Spark specialized decode", "Muse-Spark-Open recipe" and `label:recipe` "Muse".
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change and this description. The submitter reviewed the diff.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Qwen3.5: keep configuration-specific content out of the guides
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the Qwen3.5 part of vllm-project/recipes#1156. On recipes.vllm.ai the command builder renders the selected hardware and variant. The guide below it is the same static text for every selection, yet the Qwen3.5 guides held commands for a single configuration:
- a "Docker" section that was only the Intel XPU image;
- launch commands for one GPU and checkpoint;
- a client example whose `model` only the BF16 variant serves.

Readers could not tell which instructions applied to them.

This keeps the guides to what holds for every configuration. Content that is specific to a configuration moves to `notes` and `troubleshooting`, which the builder filters by the current selection.

It also fixes Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, whose builder offered no NVIDIA or AMD GPU at all.

## Claims

**Guides (all eight Qwen3.5 recipes)**

- **Removed:** the install, `docker`, and `vllm serve` blocks. The builder renders each of them for the selected configuration.
- **Kept:**
  - hardware sizing;
  - AMD measurements and explanations;
  - the MXFP4 section;
  - long context;
  - references.
- **Converted to a table:** 397B's per-workload configurations (workload, hardware, checkpoint, parallelism, other settings). Each row now names the hardware it was verified on.
- **Client examples:** they read the served name from `/v1/models` (`client.models.list().data[0].id`), so they work for every variant. This includes the Ascend variants, which set `--served-model-name qwen3.5`.
- **Thinking toggle:** the hint now sits with the client example, both per request (`chat_template_kwargs`) and per server.

**Notes and troubleshooting**

- **Notes** (shown only for a matching selection):
  - Arc Pro validation settings, including `--max-model-len 8192`, for 9B, 27B and 35B-A3B;
  - "MTP on ROCm: use an FP8 KV cache" for 397B.
- **Troubleshooting:**
  - the Mamba cache assert, on NVIDIA and AMD;
  - experimental prefix caching;
  - the CPU startup timeout (35B-A3B);
  - Encoder Parallel memory (397B).

**4B and 35B-A3B hardware**

- **The bug:** vllm-project/recipes#1029 set each variant's `supported_hardware` from the recipe's `verified` hardware, which was Xeon 6 and Arc Pro only. `supported_hardware` is an allowlist, so every other GPU was locked out of these pages, and the default page opened on Arc Pro B60.
- **The fix:**
  - BF16 has no allowlist again, so it runs everywhere. Xeon 6 and Arc remain because `meta.hardware` declares them.
  - The quantized variants list `arch:sm90/sm100/sm103/gfx942/gfx950` plus the Arc Pro ids. They still exclude Xeon, which is what #1029 wanted.

## Validation

- **Renderer check:** `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes against recipes main. `test-schema`, `test-guide-html`, `test-context` and `test-overlay` pass.
- **Rendered commands:** built against recipes main before and after this change and compared every JSON rendering (`command`, `argv`, `env`, `docker_command`, `worker_commands`).
  - No existing per-hardware rendering changed.
  - The changes are additions: 380 new renderings (NVIDIA and AMD for 4B and 35B-A3B, plus their promoted variants).
  - The default-hardware files of 35B-A3B moved from Arc Pro B60 to H200.
  - Xeon 6 still renders only the BF16 variant.
- **Builder:** checked locally.
  - 9B on Arc Pro B60 shows the validation note.
  - The 397B guide renders the configuration table and the MXFP4 section.
- **vllm-ascend overlay:** the 397B overlay carries no guide sections, so the guide edit doesn't change it.

## Details

- **Overlap with #63881.** That PR rewrites the 35B-A3B CPU install block that this PR deletes. Whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. Otherwise #63881 can drop its `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.yaml` hunk.
- **Removed outright:**
  - the 397B AMD pip note (Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, glibc ≥ 2.35);
  - its "use `cu130-nightly` on Blackwell" line.

  The builder's install block covers both, and both had gone stale.
- **Not in this PR:** the same `supported_hardware` pattern from #1029 in the other recipes it touched (Gemma 4, Llama, Phi-4, Qwen3, …), and the other guides that still carry launch commands. Those are follow-ups.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: add Rubin VR200 support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds Rubin VR200 to the Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipes, using the `vr200` profile from vllm-project/recipes#1209. Both are declared `supported`, not `verified`.

## Claims

- **Kimi-K3:** VR200 is selectable on the `default`, `nvfp4` and `fp8` variants with `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly`. It opens on `multi_node_tp` over 2 trays (8 GPUs).
- **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash:** VR200 is selectable on the `default` variant with `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash-cu134`, at TP4.
- **Scope:** this changes recipe content only. It claims no serving result or performance on Rubin.

## Validation

**These recipes have not been served on Rubin, and no model evaluation was run.** Validation covers rendering only.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` (renderer at vllm-project/recipes `main`) | Pass |
| `pnpm test:schema`, `test:overlay`, `test:presets` | All pass |
| `pnpm test:render` | 1 fail: `resolveSelection renders every preset point identically`, which also failed on an earlier renderer baseline without these recipe changes |
| JSON API before and after, about 22,590 files, ignoring source metadata | Content changes only in these two recipes and their promoted variant pages; 30 files added |

In the rendered VR200 commands, every strategy uses the expected image, and none contains `deep_gemm` or ROCm env vars. Both images publish `amd64` and `arm64`.

## Details

A recipe's `blackwell` block doesn't apply on Rubin in the renderer, and without it these recipes lose required settings such as the KV dtype and attention backend. Each recipe now shares that block with a `rubin` block through a YAML anchor.

- **Kimi-K3 backend:** `TOKENSPEED_MLA` accepts any 10.x device, which includes SM107.
- **AMD-only modes:** MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's DBO, SP and Mono decode modes were hidden by `blackwell: unsupported`, so they now also set `rubin: unsupported`.
- **Not carried over:** GB200/GB300 MegaMoE, the tuned PD configurations, the AgentX presets and Kimi-K3's `multi_node_tp_dp`, none of which have been run on Rubin. PD on VR200 therefore renders the plain baseline.

**Where review is needed:**

- **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash image:** `minimax-m31-flash-cu134` is a local build (its labels report commit `unknown`, created 2026-10-22), so I couldn't confirm it supports these flags, in particular NVFP4 KV with the `FLASHINFER_TS` DSpark draft.
- **MSA on Rubin:** the [Rubin preview post](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-09-vera-rubin-preview) lists the Rubin MSA decode kernels as unfinished and describes FP8 KV for MiniMax M3.
- **Image note on the page:** the renderer's Rubin note says only the nightly image runs on this hardware, which also shows beside MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's dedicated image. That text lives in vllm-project/recipes.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching these two recipes cover Ascend variants, env cleanup, ROCm TP2 and GB300 presets, and none adds Rubin.

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector] Reuse the Mooncake PD TransferEngine in the store connector
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Opt-in `reuse_pd_transfer_engine` lets `MooncakeStoreConnector` attach to the TransferEngine `MooncakeConnector` already created in the same worker, instead of initializing a second one.

No open PR covers this; #38474 (closed Store Connector RFC) and #47302 (encoder-cache store path) do not share the PD engine.

## Claims

- One TransferEngine per worker serves both PD and KV-store traffic: no second RDMA init, GPU KV registration, P2P handshake endpoint or CPU segment mount.
- When reusing, the store registers no KV buffers; device and HiSparse host KV stay registered by `MooncakeConnector`, so store-side sleep/wake is a no-op and sleep eligibility is decided by `MooncakeConnector.supports_sleep_mode`.
- Default behavior is unchanged without the flag.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -q   # 418 passed
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main...HEAD)    # passed
```

No Mooncake RDMA CI job exists. Local E2E on 2× H20 (GPU 0 prefill, GPU 1 decode), `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, PD `P2PHANDSHAKE`/`rdma`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Engine inits per side | reuse: 1 + `Skip its initialization`; separate: 2 |
| Proxied chat "17 + 25" | `42` in both modes |
| 16 req, in 128 / out 32, conc 2 | reuse 5.60 req/s, TTFT 65.6 ms; separate 5.59 req/s, TTFT 69.9 ms |
| D-side `sleep(1)` → `wake_up`, store JSON without `device_name`, `protocol: tcp` | request returns `42`; no `ERR_ADDRESS_OVERLAPPED` |
| Store listed before `MooncakeConnector` | fails with `no MooncakeConnector TransferEngine` |

<details>
<summary>GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot, temp 0, seed 42; measured on the first revision, data path unchanged since)</summary>

| Mode | Accuracy | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Reuse | 0.3268 | 200.0s |
| Separate | 0.3237 | 199.8s |

</details>

## Details

- `MooncakeConnectorWorker` publishes its engine in a single-slot, process-local registry after `initialize()`. One worker process holds at most one PD worker and all accesses run from serialized lifecycle calls, so there is no device key and no lock. `clear` only drops the slot when it still points at the engine being shut down.
- The store calls `setup(engine=TransferEngine.get_engine())`. Mooncake then skips engine init, resolves an empty `metadata_server` from the engine, and ignores `rdma_devices`; the store passes the PD protocol and `hostname:rpc_port`. The store JSON's `metadata_server`, `protocol` and `device_name` therefore do not apply to the shared engine. `MooncakeConnector` must be listed first.
- Both connectors register KV per untyped storage and the store's layers (`prefix_cacheable_groups`) ⊆ PD layers (`transfer_groups`, which include the HiSparse host source group), so the store skips KV registration entirely when reusing. The store's `device_name`/`device_name_per_gpu` are not resolved when an engine is supplied.
- A Mooncake build whose `setup()` lacks `engine=` fails with an upgrade error. Store `close()` drops its reference; the engine is owned by `MooncakeConnector`. Deployments wanting a separate NIC for the store should omit the flag.

AI assistance was used; the author reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Split the platform and stat logger plugin tests out of Plugin Integration and shard it
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (CI YAML only, one file).

Plugin Integration installs and uninstalls a plugin around each test file, so its commands aren't plain pytest and it can't use automatic sharding. This PR moves the two plugins that act on every vLLM process (the dummy platform and the dummy stat logger) into their own step. The rest install together up front, which leaves Plugin Integration with plain pytest commands, so it and its MI250 mirror enroll in automatic sharding.

## Claims

- Plugin Integration (L4) and its MI250 mirror are enrolled with `automatic_shard: true`. Both plan one shard today, so their jobs don't change; they shard on their own when the tests grow.
- Every test that ran before still runs: 10 pytest commands stay in Plugin Integration, in main's order, and 2 move to the new step.
- New step "Platform and Stat Logger Plugins" (L4 + MI250 mirror) runs as one job, with main's install, test and uninstall lines.

## Validation

- Planned with the pipeline generator on ci-infra main: one shard on each platform.
- `/ci run` build 101561 on this head passed all four jobs: Plugin Integration and Platform and Stat Logger Plugins, on both platforms. Build 101547, on the previous head with the same change, passed too.
- Node IDs against main build 101458 (no plugin test change between them): 65 on each platform in both PR builds, with 0 missing, 0 added, 0 changed outcomes and 0 duplicates.
- Peer review (Codex): no issues.

## Details

- **Why two plugins move out:** with `VLLM_PLUGINS` unset, an installed stat logger plugin loads in every engine and turns stats on (`AsyncLLM` with custom loggers), and the dummy platform replaces the platform in every process. The other five act only when a test names them (io_processor and endpoint plugins), or only add new model names (dummy model), so installing them together changes nothing for the other tests.
- **Simplest option turned down:** reordering the commands so all installs come first, in one step. That keeps the stat logger and dummy platform active for every later test.
- **Source dependencies:** the import-time platform files (`vllm/__init__.py`, `vllm/platforms/__init__.py`, and the others) now trigger only the new step, since they were there for the platform test. Plugin Integration keeps `vllm/plugins/` and `tests/plugins/` (plus `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` on AMD).
- **Cost:** the new step is one more job per platform, so each run repeats one job's setup, a few minutes of machine time. That is the price of keeping the stat logger and dummy platform away from the other tests.
- Timeouts stay as on main.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Enroll Language Models (Extended Generation) in automatic sharding; spawn in test_gemma's dummy-loader test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Trunk change: needs line-by-line review** (it changes how a CI step's tests are split across jobs).

Enrolls Language Models (Extended Generation) and its AMD mirror in `automatic_shard`, and fixes the one test that failed once the step was sharded. It needed #58795 (merged), which moved the mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d builds into the test image. Split out of #64604, which enrolls the other Language Models steps that built them.

## Claims

- `test_gemma.py::test_dummy_loader` no longer depends on running after another file: it sets `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` itself, the mode it already ran under in the full step.
- Extended Generation and its AMD mirror shard automatically, and every test main runs still runs exactly once.
- The step finishes in about a quarter of main's single-job time, each shard under the 20-minute target, for about a fifth more machine time (see Details).

## Validation

- **Without the fix** (scoped build [100348](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100348), with this step enrolled): the shard that ran `test_gemma.py` on its own failed all three `test_dummy_loader` cases at engine start:
  ```
  torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: initialization error
  FAILED models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_dummy_loader[google/gemma-2b] - RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
  ```
  In main's nightly [100175](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175) the step runs as one job and the same tests pass: while `test_common.py` runs, before `test_gemma.py`, vLLM logs `Overriding VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD to 'spawn'`, and the setting stays for the rest of the process.
- **With the fix** (scoped build [100358](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100358)): the plan again put `test_gemma.py` alone in one shard, and that shard passed with no CUDA initialization error (`11 passed, 43 deselected`).
- **This head:** [`/ci run` 101610](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101610) plus scoped build [101611](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101611) for the AMD mirror, which `/ci run` leaves out. Every shard passed with no retries. Against main daily build [101548](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101548): 51 node IDs on NVIDIA and 75 on AMD, none missing, added, duplicated or with a changed outcome. The same holds against this PR's builds from before the `--ignore` change (101583, 101594).
- `split_check.py`: no step runs its whole suite in each of its jobs. pytest collection of `test_gdn_sleep_wake.py` before and after its marker change: 1 test under `-m hybrid_model`, none under this step's filter.

## Details

- **Root cause:** in the full step an earlier file leaves the process on spawn, so `test_dummy_loader` never forked. Run first in its own process, as a shard can run it, its engine forks and the child can't initialize CUDA. Which earlier call put CUDA in use in the parent isn't pinned down; spawn works either way, as the full step shows.
- **`--ignore` for `test_hybrid.py` and `test_gdn_sleep_wake.py`:** every test in them is `hybrid_model`, which this step's filter excludes, so main never times them and the planner counted each as a median-sized file. That planned one shard per platform that ran no tests. Ignoring them leaves the selected tests unchanged and the plan one shard smaller on each platform. `test_gdn_sleep_wake.py` now marks `hybrid_model` at module level, like `test_hybrid.py`, so a test added to either file later still runs in the Hybrid step.
- **Machine time is about a fifth above main** on both platforms: each shard starts a fresh process and reloads its models, which the single job did once. Accepted for the shorter wall time.
- **Timeouts unchanged.**
- **Not fixed here:** `test_common.py::test_models[...HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B]` intermittently fails on main with "No available memory for the cache blocks"; it is unrelated to sharding.
- No other open PR enrolls this step. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Let DomynEdge mix sliding and full attention layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]` fails on every CI run that collects it since `domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base` updated its config on the Hub (2026-11-10 12:06 UTC). The new config sets `layer_types` with both sliding and full attention layers, which `Qwen2Model` rejects. DomynEdge already applies each layer's window itself, so this lets it skip that check.

## Claims

- `test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]` no longer fails on `Sliding window for some but all layers is not supported`.
- No behavior change for any other `Qwen2Model` subclass (Qwen2, Qwen3, MiMo, DeepSeek-V4, ...): the check still runs for them.
- No change to how DomynEdge computes attention: its layers already take their windows from `config.window_sizes`.

## Validation

Seen on both platforms in https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101457, unchanged after a retry:

```
AssertionError: Sliding window for some but all layers is not supported. This model uses sliding window but `max_window_layers` = 36 is less than `num_hidden_layers` = 1.
FAILED models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]
```

This PR has not been run on a GPU locally; the reproducer is `pytest models/test_initialization.py -k DomynEdgeForCausalLM`, which runs in the Basic Models (Extra Initialization) jobs. `tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py` (`domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base`, vLLM vs HF logprobs) covers the full model with the new config.

Checked statically:
- In the new config, `window_sizes` (derived from `layer_types` by the remote `DomynEdgeConfig`) marks exactly the `sliding_attention` layers, all with `(1024, 0)`, and `sliding_window = 1025`. `DomynEdgeAttention` passes `window_size + 1 = 1025` as `per_layer_sliding_window` on those layers and `None` on full attention layers.
- Full attention layers do not pick up the model-level window: `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` only sets `CacheConfig.sliding_window` when every entry of `layer_types` is `sliding_attention`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `check-docstring-style`: clean.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Qwen2Model.__init__` asserts `max_window_layers == num_hidden_layers` whenever `layer_types` has more than one value, because `Qwen2DecoderLayer` cannot apply a per-layer window. The remote `DomynEdgeConfig` defaults `max_window_layers` to `num_hidden_layers` only to get past this check (its comment: "remove once vLLM's native DomynEdge no longer requires it ... in Domyn Edge `layer_types` alone decides which layers slide"). A full model therefore loads, but `test_can_initialize` overrides `num_hidden_layers` to 1 after the config is built, leaving `max_window_layers = 36`.

**Fix.** A `supports_per_layer_sliding_window` class attribute on `Qwen2Model`, `False` by default, guards the check. `DomynEdgeModel` sets it to `True`.

**Why not pin the checkpoint revision** in `tests/models/registry.py`: the Hub repo history was rewritten and now has a single commit, so no earlier revision exists.

|---|---|---|
| `language-models-tests-hybrid` | fixed 2-way split becomes automatic | same |

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Rust][Benchmark] Reuse allowed tokens in multi-turn generation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Multi-turn synthetic dataset generation rebuilt the tokenizer's allowed-token
list whenever an encode/decode round trip produced fewer tokens than the target
length.

Reuse the list already computed at dataset initialization to avoid repeated
vocabulary scans and temporary allocations during retries.



## Claims

- Reuse one allowed-token list across normal and prefix-sharing generation.
- Eliminate repeated vocabulary scans during prompt-length retries.
- Preserve prompt generation behavior and token-selection order.
- Reduce dataset preparation time by 33.2% in the measured large-vocabulary
  local-tokenizer workload.



## Validation


Benchmark configuration:

- Tokenizer: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
- 1,000 conversations
- 3 turns per conversation
- 512 input tokens per turn
- One Rayon worker
- Release build
- Five runs using seeds 0 through 4

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| get_allowed_tokens calls | 182 | 1 | -181 |
| Generation time, mean ± stddev | 5.018 ± 0.095 s | 3.353 ± 0.023 s | -33.2% |
| Average process wall time | 5.122 s | 3.464 s | -32.4% |
| Average user CPU time | 5.080 s | 3.434 s | -32.4% |

The generation-time speedup is 1.50x for this workload. The measurement covers
synthetic dataset preparation, not model serving or inference throughput.

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench  --all-targets --all-features  --locked  -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run -p vllm-bench --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo test -p vllm-bench  --all-features --locked --  --ignored
cargo build -p vllm-bench --release --locked

```



## Details



generate_multi_turn_random already computes the allowed-token list once
before generating conversations. However, gen_prompt_to_target_len
previously called get_allowed_tokens again whenever an encode/decode
round-trip produced fewer tokens than requested.

For large local tokenizers, each retry traversed the vocabulary and allocated
a new Vec<u32>. A Qwen tokenizer with 151,665 vocabulary entries allocated
approximately 1 MiB for each reconstruction.

The prompt-length helper now accepts the existing list as a borrowed
&[u32]. All five call paths pass the same immutable list:

- normal multi-turn prompts
- global shared prefixes
- per-conversation prefixes
- per-turn unique suffixes
- optional random shared prefixes

The tokenizer remains immutable during generation, so every previous
reconstruction produced the same ordered list. Reusing it does not change
token selection, prompt contents, retry behavior, CLI options, or output
formats.

The benefit is largest for local large-vocabulary tokenizers whose
get_allowed_tokens implementation filters every vocabulary entry. Built-in
tokenizers have a cheaper construction path and therefore see a smaller
improvement.

## Overview

Fix the XPU Rust frontend external-LB test introduced by #56246 by keeping all node XPUs visible to every externally launched DP rank.

Same issue with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53037
Buildkite failure: [build 17067, Rust Frontend Distributed](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/17067#01a1baff-0c77-44c5-870c-1a44f53ce261)
## Claims

- Prevent oneCCL topology discovery from hanging when external DP ranks run in
  separate server processes.
- Preserve the existing per-rank visibility behavior on non-XPU platforms.


## Details

The test assigned a single `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` device to each external DP
process. Unlike the CUDA path, XPU external-LB workers require every rank to
see the complete node device set so oneCCL can discover the communicator
topology. The XPU worker already maps each external DP index onto its device,
so this change lets child processes inherit the job's full XPU mask while
retaining explicit per-rank masks elsewhere.

#56246 is the confirmed exposure trigger: it added this XPU Rust frontend job,
which failed in all three runs since introduction. No open PR or issue found by
searching the test name, external-LB/XPU affinity keywords, and recent XPU PRs
duplicates this fix.

AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, and validate this change. A
human must review every changed line before marking this draft ready.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Rust Frontend] Serialize SSE chunks before building the event
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Build streamed SSE frames with `Event::data(serde_json::to_string(..))` instead of `Event::json_data(..)` in the chat completions, completions, generate and Responses routes. Same wire bytes, 1.9–2.7× less time per frame.

The serialization lives in one `EventExt::json` helper next to `sse_response`, whose doc records why it avoids `json_data`. The three identical chat completions, completions and generate SSE stream functions are merged into one generic `openai_sse_stream`.

## Claims

- Per-frame SSE serialization is 46–62% faster (criterion bench table below).
- Wire output is byte-identical
- Heap operations per frame are not increased (5–7 on both paths)
- Reach: every streaming request on the Rust frontend

## Validation

Criterion, axum 0.8.8, Apple M-series, mimalloc, `critcmp` over one run (both variants in one binary and every case first asserts identical wire bytes through axum's `Sse` response):

| case | `json_data` (old) | `data(to_string)` (new) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| content_token | 504.8 ns | 224.4 ns | 2.25× |
| reasoning_token | 503.7 ns | 223.2 ns | 2.26× |
| first_role | 554.3 ns | 246.6 ns | 2.25× |
| content_escapes | 557.8 ns | 239.3 ns | 2.33× |
| content_120B | 568.0 ns | 305.4 ns | 1.86× |
| finish | 616.0 ns | 254.6 ns | 2.42× |
| tool_args | 693.4 ns | 275.5 ns | 2.52× |
| logprobs_top5_token_ids | 2.13 µs | 799.7 ns | 2.66× |

Intervals were within ±1%, and a repeat run reproduced each variant within ~1%.

End to end, `vllm-rs` + `vllm-mock-engine` + `vllm-bench` (streaming chat, 2048 requests, 3 alternated rounds) showed about −8% server CPU and +6% req/s. That run was on a shared laptop under load, so treat it as directional only. I have no GPU end-to-end number.

Tests:

```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server                        # 655 passed, 0 skipped
cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo fmt --check                                       # clean
```

No new tests. This is a behavior preserving change, and the existing route tests already parse the streamed `data:` lines. Byte identity was checked separately against the real chunk types (above). Evals: not applicable. Output bytes are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: searched open and closed PRs for `json_data`, `Event::data`, "Rust Frontend SSE" and "SSE serialization". The open PRs that touch these route files (#63926, #63739, #61275, #64573, #63481, #58783) do not edit these lines.

## Details

serde_json writes a chunk as dozens of small fragments; a typical 230-byte chat chunk takes 77 `write` calls, 59 of them 1–2 bytes. `json_data` passes each fragment straight to axum's `EventDataWriter::write_buf`, which repeats a newline/CR scan, a flag check and a `BytesMut` reserve per fragment, and regrows the buffer from capacity 0 as fragments arrive. Serializing into a `Vec` first makes those writes an inlined memcpy, and `data()` does one scan and one copy.

The cost is one extra temporary `String` per frame. The event buffer then grows in fewer steps, so total heap operations stay the same or drop by one. Output is identical because compact serde_json never emits a raw `\n` or `\r`.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this target while profiling the Rust frontend against the mock engine, draft the patch, and build the benchmark and identity check. I reviewed every line, traced where the win comes from in axum's and serde_json's source, and re-ran the tests and benchmarks above myself. I can answer for the change.
