commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix cancellation during request submission
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a race in the Rust frontend where cancelling a request during submission can send `Abort` before `Add`, allowing the engine to process a request that the caller has already cancelled.

## Claims

- Keep the output stream alive in the spawned Add send task until the send completes, preventing cancellation from enqueueing Abort before Add.
- Add a deterministic regression test that cancels the caller after the send task is spawned but before it runs.

## Validation

Validated on the development machine with Rust 1.95.

- The regression test fails on the base implementation and passes with this change.
- The baseline run used a test-only adaptation for the original `send_request_to_engine()` signature; no production code was changed.
- **154 passed, 0 failed** in the Rust engine-core client test suite.
- Clippy, formatting and applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Baseline regression-test failure:

```text
assertion failed: matches!(abort_rx.try_recv(), Err(mpsc::error::TryRecvError::Empty))
test client::imp::tests::cancelling_add_defers_abort_until_send_completes ... FAILED
```

Validation commands from `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-features

cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

The regression test is covered by the existing Rust Frontend Cargo CPU CI job.

## Details

Add is sent by a spawned task that continues running when its caller is cancelled. Previously, cancellation dropped the output stream in the caller and triggered auto-abort while Add could still be pending. The scheduler ignores aborts for unknown request IDs, so an Abort received before Add does not prevent the subsequent Add from starting generation.

Move the output stream into the existing send task and return it after the send completes. If the caller has already been cancelled, the returned stream is dropped when the send task completes, triggering auto-abort. The existing send-error registration rollback remains in place.

---

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector] Let external connectors declare KV cache memory registration
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Lets out-of-tree KV connectors (loaded through `kv_connector_module_path`) declare that they register the device KV cache for RDMA. The extensible KV cache (#56492) then backs each segment with a single physical allocation for them too, as it already does for the in-tree NIXL, Mooncake, MoRIIO and UMBP connectors (#65210, #65225).

## Claims

- New classmethod `KVConnectorBase_V1.registers_kv_cache_memory(kv_transfer_config)`, default `False`, placed next to `supports_lookahead_block_hashes`.
- `KVTransferConfig.registers_kv_cache_memory()` also returns `True` when an external connector's classmethod says so, whether it is configured directly or inside `MultiConnector`. `MultiConnector` overrides the classmethod and delegates to its children.
- In-tree connectors keep using `_KV_CACHE_REGISTERING_CONNECTORS`, so their behavior is unchanged. A direct in-tree connector is not imported by this check.
- Without this, an external RDMA connector can't start with the extensible KV cache, which is on by default with the V2 model runner. The cache is committed in several physical chunks, and `ibv_reg_mr` rejects the range. The only workaround is `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue lets external connectors opt in. #65210 (closed) and #65225 (merged) limit alignment and defragmentation to the in-tree name list. #65507 special-cases LMCache MP through a config key and handles exported VMM handles rather than RDMA registration. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed every changed line.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty` editable install, macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py -k registers_kv_cache_memory
# 22 passed (18 existing + 4 new)
# with the vllm/ changes reverted and the tests kept: 2 failed (both RegistersKVCacheTestConnector cases), 20 passed

pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py
# 92 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed
```

- The one failure is `test_multi_example_connector_consistency`. It downloads the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` (HF 401 in my environment) and is unrelated to this change.
- `test_multi_connector_overrides_all_base_methods` passes because `MultiConnector` now overrides the new classmethod.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, including mypy, check-test-tethering and validate-config.

**End to end** (8x H800, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8 + EP, MTP, V2 model runner, extensible KV cache on by default) with the external dfkv connector ([dingodb/DingoCache](https://github.com/dingodb/DingoCache), `DfkvStoreConnector` via `kv_connector_module_path`). It registers the KV cache with `ibv_reg_mr` through GPUDirect RDMA.

> This ran on our downstream vLLM build, a fork of a recent main (2026-11), with this PR's hook ported onto it. I did not run this hardware on unmodified upstream main.

| vLLM | Result |
|---|---|
| unmodified | `ibv_reg_mr` on the multi-chunk KV range fails and startup aborts |
| with this hook, connector declares `registers_kv_cache_memory = True` (connector side: dingodb/DingoCache#412) | `registers_kv_cache_memory() = True` (`DfkvStoreConnector` not on the name list); `Extended KV cache to 3280 blocks (24.88 GiB)` on all 8 ranks; a single 25474 MiB RDMA registration per rail; requests served, 39/39 KV puts succeeded |

## Details

- **Why a classmethod rather than more names on the list.** The list can only name connectors that live in this repository. Every external RDMA connector would otherwise need a vLLM PR, or would have to run without the extensible KV cache. The classmethod follows the existing `supports_lookahead_block_hashes` and `supports_sleep_mode` pattern, so a connector describes its own needs.
- **Why the name list stays.** Moving the in-tree connectors onto the classmethod is possible, but it would turn this fix into a refactor of five connectors and change when their modules are imported. I kept the scope minimal and can do that as a follow-up if reviewers prefer one mechanism.
- **Where it runs.** `registers_kv_cache_memory()` is called by the worker when it sizes and commits the extensible KV cache, and on ROCm during config validation. Resolving an external class imports its module, as `MultiConnector` already does for `supports_lookahead_block_hashes`.
- **Docs.** The classmethod docstring documents the contract. The `enable_extensible_kv_cache` docstring, which generates the CLI and config reference, now points external connector authors to it.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][MiniMax-M3] Allow the BLHNC KV cache layout with an NVFP4 KV cache
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Let the MiniMax-M3 MSA NVFP4 backend run on the `BLHNC` KV cache layout. It declared only `LBHNC`, so `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` failed at layout resolution on NVIDIA with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`.

## Claims

- `MiniMaxM3SparseMSANvfp4Backend` accepts `BLHNC` in addition to `LBHNC`. `LBHNC` stays first, so the default layout does not change.
- With `BLHNC`, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector registers one block-strided region per rank and copies one row per block, instead of one page per layer (about 120 pages of 9–18 KB each on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4).
- GSM8K accuracy holds on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with NVFP4 KV + `BLHNC`, including KV loaded back from CPU.

## Validation

GB200, TP4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`, NVFP4 indexer, DSpark (7 tokens), SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (eager), `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`. `--num-gpu-blocks-override 2048` caps the GPU pool at 262k tokens, so the second GSM8K pass reloads evicted prefixes from CPU. Commit `4e3463c874` plus this change (its csrc is identical to main).

| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions | flexible | strict | request errors | external (CPU) prefix hit rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pass 1 (stores to CPU) | 95.53 | 95.38 | 0 | ~1% |
| pass 2 (loads from CPU) | 95.30 | 95.07 | 0 | 93% at the end of the pass |

The engine log shows `Using BLHNC KV cache layout.` and `SimpleCPUOffloadWorker [CPU]: 1 tensors, 27431 CPU blocks (46.57 GB)` per rank.

<details>
<summary>Serve command</summary>

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --language-model-only --trust-remote-code --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --num-gpu-blocks-override 2048 \
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_TS","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":50000000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
```

GSM8K ran twice back to back with 5 shots, temperature 0, max_tokens 1024 and concurrency 64.
</details>

`pre-commit` passes. No unit test covers the backend's layout list. CI has no GB200 job that serves this model, so the validation above ran outside CI.

## Details

The NVFP4 MSA kernels need each head's K/V slots to be one contiguous run of a page. `BLHNC` keeps that property and only widens the page stride to a full block row. Every NVFP4 path takes the page stride from the cache view: the fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV insert (`kv_s_block`, int64), the fused QKV epilogue (dynamic int64 page stride), `nvfp4_head_slot_views` (`k.stride(0)`), the NVFP4 index-K gather (int64 page offsets) and the fmha_sm100 Q8KV4 decode/prefill (`nvfp4_page_stride`, int64).

Limitations:
- NIXL P/D with `BLHNC` + NVFP4 KV on NVIDIA was not run. NIXL still registers one strided region per layer for this GQA model, so it does not reduce descriptors yet.
- No performance A/B against `LBHNC` was run. The PR claims only correctness and the copy granularity of SimpleCPUOffloadConnector.
- ROCm uses a separate NVFP4 backend and is not affected.

Duplicate check: no open PR changes the MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 layout list (searched "MiniMax BLHNC", "minimax nvfp4 layout", "NVFP4 BLHNC"). #65885 caches the NVFP4 KV views and keeps their strides, so it is compatible.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Mono decode layer for Kimi-K3 on MI355X w/ vanilla decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Extend Kimi-K3's MI355X MonoKernel from [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) to support ordinary autoregressive decode without speculative decoding.

This is a stacked extension of [#60683](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683) and should merge only after that PR.

## Claims

- Supports pure, uniform regular-decode steps with widths 1–16 (`MAX_ROWS`).
- Preserves the existing speculative-verification path.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Key the FSE MXFP8 scale-layout test check on the selected backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `test_fse_online_quantization_routed_shared` so it checks the MXFP8 scale layout of the backend that was actually selected. The three `routed_mxfp8` cases fail on gfx942 (MI300) because the test assumes every MXFP8 backend stores flattened scales. This is a test-only change. It lets the three MI300 `--deselect` flags in #66672 be removed.

Fixes: <!-- issue link to be filled -->

## Claims

- Fixes the 3 `routed_mxfp8` failures (`assert 4 == (4 * 512)`) on any ROCm GPU where `supports_mx()` is False (gfx942), or where AITER fused MoE or flydsl is unavailable.
- Keeps the flattened-layout check on the AITER_MXFP8 (FlyDSL) path, where that layout is produced.
- Does not change vLLM runtime behaviour.

## Validation

All runs were on MI355X (gfx950), from `tests/`, with `W=<worktree>` and torchao placed off the default path as in #66672 (`/tmp/qdeps`). gfx942 was **simulated** with a pytest plugin that patches the platform at `pytest_configure`. No real MI300 run was done.

| Configuration | Command | Before (`b76e2401f8`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fuller gfx942 simulation (`rocm._ON_GFX950=False`, `_ON_GFX942=True`, `supports_mx()=False`; MXFP4 and MXFP8 both select EMULATION) | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=$W:/tmp/qdeps:<plugin dir> python -m pytest -p <plugin> quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -q` | 3 failed, 43 passed, 3 skipped | 46 passed, 3 skipped |
| `supports_mx()=False` only | same, with the `force_no_mx` plugin | 3 failed, 44 passed, 2 skipped | 47 passed, 2 skipped |
| Native gfx950 (AITER_MXFP8, no forcing) | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=$W:/tmp/qdeps python -m pytest quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -q` | 47 passed, 2 skipped | 47 passed, 2 skipped |
| gfx950 with `moe_backend="triton"` forced (TRITON_MXFP8) | `-k routed_mxfp8` | 3 failed | 3 passed |

In each "before" row the failures are exactly `[nvfp4_routed_mxfp8_shared-routed_mxfp8]`, `[quark_nvfp4_routed_bf16_shared-routed_mxfp8]` and `[quark_nvfp4_routed_nvfp4_shared-routed_mxfp8]`, each failing with `assert 4 == (4 * 512)`. These are the same three ids that #66672 deselects on MI300.

Scale shapes logged during the runs:
- Native gfx950: MXFP8 uses AITER_MXFP8 with flattened scales `(2048, 8)` / `(1024, 8)`, so the flattened check still runs there. MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX use AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4 with 3-D scales `(N, 512, 8)`.
- Simulated gfx942: every case uses EMULATION with 3-D scales `(N, 512, 8)` / `(N, 256, 8)`.

Lint: `pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` passes.

**Not covered locally:** I did not run this on real gfx942/MI300 hardware. I validated it with the simulation above, and the MI300 Quantization job in #66672 will exercise it. NVIDIA does not apply: the module has `pytestmark = skipif(not current_platform.is_rocm())`. No csrc is involved.

## Details

**Root cause.** For every `Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod`, the test asserted the flattened layout `w13_weight_scale.shape[0] == num_slots * w13_weight.shape[1]`. Only AITER_MXFP8 produces that layout. In `oracle/fp8.py`, `convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format` calls `rocm_aiter_ops.shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights` only for that backend, and that function reshapes the scales to `(-1, K // 32)`. `select_mxfp8_moe_backend` (`oracle/mxfp8.py`) picks the first supported backend. AITER_MXFP8 and TRITON_MXFP8 both need `current_platform.supports_mx()`, which is False on gfx942, so EMULATION is selected there. EMULATION keeps 3-D `[num_slots, rows, K // 32]` scales, so `shape[0] == num_slots` and the assertion fails. Forcing only `supports_mx()=False` on gfx950 reproduces the failure exactly, which shows that fnuz FP8 and the gfx942 arch flags play no part.

**Culprit.** #64378 (`2abde627d9`, "[ROCm][Quantization] NVFP4 MoE re-quantization and fused shared experts through online quantization") added the `routed_mxfp8` case and the class-keyed flattened assertion. Pickaxe on `routed_method_cls is Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod` finds only that commit. It merged on 2026-10-29, after the ROCm Quantization job was disabled on 2026-10-25 by #63608 (`9d48c8ab95`), so the test never ran on MI300. A bisect is not meaningful because the failing assertion was introduced together with the test.

**Fix.** The flattened layout is checked only when `quant_method.fp8_backend == Fp8MoeBackend.AITER_MXFP8`. Every other case (EMULATION, TRITON_MXFP8, and the MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX methods, which have no `fp8_backend`) asserts `w13/w2_weight_scale.shape[0] == num_slots`. The MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX routed cases had no scale-shape check before, so this PR also makes them stricter. The check holds for AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4 and EMULATION. If a future MXFP4 backend flattens its scales, this branch will need updating. Diff: +6/-2, test only.

**Related PRs.**
- #66672: with this PR merged, the three `--deselect='...routed_mxfp8]'` flags can be removed from the MI300 Quantization step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and from its mirror in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml`.
- #66803 edits a different line of the same file (around L1433, `NvFp4MoeBackend.EMULATION` to `NONE`). At most a trivial rebase is expected and no conflict.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `test_online_shared_expert_fusion` (no results), `routed_mxfp8` (only #66672, which deselects these tests rather than fixing them), `mxfp8 scale layout`, `mxfp8 scale shape shared expert fusion` and `w13_weight_scale num_slots`. None of the other hits (for example #65479, #65421, #57977, #63203, #66771) touch this test.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Security] muse: fix quadratic attribute scans in tool-call extraction
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bound Muse's ATEM attribute scans to a single tag and avoid reparsing tool calls on streaming deltas that cannot complete an invocation. This updates the existing fix after review; it does not add a separate parser or change the shared parser interface.

## Claims

- Attribute searches stop at the next `<` instead of scanning across repeated unterminated tags.
- Tool-call parsing runs when a delta completes `</atem:invoke>`, including split delimiters and the initial handoff. The emitted-call cursor never moves backwards between invocations.
- The rebase preserves #64518's `_parameter_types(request)` handling, including union, enum and `$ref` schemas.

## Validation

Rebased onto `81f1baa7318155cddfb45968c5ae1cf34fcb5ca0` on November 3. Fresh local validation uses the source parser and real vLLM protocol classes, Python 3.12.4 and torch 2.13.0+cu130:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py
# 139 passed in 47.13s, with repository conftests

ruff check vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py
ruff format --check vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py
git diff --check 81f1baa7318155cddfb45968c5ae1cf34fcb5ca0
# all passed (Ruff 0.14.0)
```

The pytest command ran through `uv run --no-project --python <existing-venv>/bin/python --with orjson`; the temporary dependency overlay leaves the shared environment unchanged. No protocol or tokenizer import stubs were used. Existing tests cover schema typing, parallel calls, channel routing and split streaming markers. The new streaming regression constructs a real `ChatCompletionRequest`; its counter wraps and calls the original parser implementation. A separate direct-parser run with `--noconftest` also passed all 139 tests.

Negative control: copied the two regression tests into an isolated upstream `ab9f51f1010ce94f572ba916ef84d8d90f519dea` checkout and ran:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/tool_use/test_muse.py \
  -k 'attribute_scan_stops_at_the_tag_boundary or streaming_parses_once_per_completed_invoke'
# FAILED test_attribute_scan_stops_at_the_tag_boundary:
#   repeated open tags incorrectly match the name attribute
# FAILED test_streaming_parses_once_per_completed_invoke:
#   AssertionError: pad=0 chunk=1: parsed 217x over 218 deltas
# 2 failed, 112 deselected
```

Both pass with this fix. The two additional upstream commits through `81f1baa731` only change ROCm build/CI files; the parser, test files and type-check configuration are identical to the tested upstream base.

Type-check comparison: `python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11 vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py` with mypy 1.20.2 and the pinned hook dependencies reports one `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`/`TokenizerLike` constructor error on both upstream (line 205) and this head (line 211). No additional errors appear in the changed files; this is not a passing type-check result.

Validation limits: tests use the supported CPU target because the source-tree GPU native extension is unavailable. No Muse checkpoint/tokenizer or live serving evaluation was available, so this is not an end-to-end serving or GPU test result. Buildkite's entrypoints API-server-generate step selects `tool_use` and depends on both changed paths; fresh remote CI remains separate from local results.

## Details

The attribute classes previously allowed `<`, so a failed attribute search could restart at each open tag and rescan the remaining suffix. Restricting those classes to `[^<>]` preserves ordinary ATEM attributes while stopping that cross-tag search.

An invocation cannot be returned before its closing tag. The streaming gate checks a window extending `len(close) - 1` characters before the new delta, so delimiters split across deltas still trigger parsing. `max(previous_count, len(calls))` preserves the emission cursor on deltas that do not parse.

The merge conflict was caused by #64518 replacing `_string_parameters()` with schema-aware `_parameter_types()`. The rebased gate calls the new helper; none of that upstream schema logic is reverted.

This does **not** make total streaming work linear: `_visible_channels(current_text)` still runs on every delta, and `_INVOKE_RE` is unchanged. No engine, scheduler, model-runner or GPU synchronization code changes.

<details>
<summary>Historical performance evidence from the pre-rebase implementation</summary>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Take openai-audio input tokens from server usage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve --backend openai-audio` reports the wrong input token count for every transcription request. The audio datasets set `prompt_len` from a text prompt the request never sends, and the client ignores `usage.prompt_tokens`. This reads `prompt_tokens` from the usage chunk, as the completions and chat clients already do.

## Claims

- On Whisper the bench reported 8 input tokens per request, the tokens of the dataset prompt "Transcribe the audio.". The server reports `100 × audio seconds + 4` (304 for a 3 s clip, 2,504 for 25 s).
- Total input tokens now match the server. Output tokens were already correct.

## Validation

New test in `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, over the completions, chat and audio clients: `prompt_len` takes the server's usage value. It fails for audio on `main`. `tests/benchmarks/` passes (194) and pre-commit is clean.

RTX 3080, `openai/whisper-tiny`, 18 clips from 3 s to 25 s cut from vLLM's `mary_had_lamb` and `winning_call` test assets, `--dataset-name custom_audio`:

| | `main` | this branch | server `usage.prompt_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| total input tokens | 144 | 21,757 | 21,757 |

Total token throughput is computed from total input tokens, so it rises with this change. Request rate and output tokens are unchanged. The request on the wire carries no prompt field.

## Details

The server's `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` metric rose by 72 on the same run, 4 per request, so it counts the decoder prompt without the audio, while `usage` counts both. I left that alone; the bench follows `usage` as it does for the other backends.

The legacy `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py` reads `prompt_tokens` for no backend, so it is out of scope.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and test. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: add GB300 AgentX presets, align with InferenceX#4907
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GB300 presets for the Dynamo + vLLM AgentX lanes of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4907](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4907), so that the recipe documents the lane's serving settings.

## Claims

| Preset | Concurrency | Layout | Image |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gb300_agentx_pd` | 20, 32, 56 | 1P3D. TP8 + DCP8 prefill with EP8 MegaMoE; TP8 + DCP8 decode on the low-latency decode backend | `kimi-k31-mc@sha256:f29efae1…` |
| `gb300_agentx_pd_hybrid` | 192, 384 | 2P1D / 3P1D. TP8 + DCP8 prefill; one decode worker of four TP8 + DCP8 engines (data-parallel 4) with EP32 MegaMoE | `kimi-k31-mc@sha256:f29efae1…` |
| `gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` | 352 | 1P1D. DEP16 prefill and decode, explicit KV cache size and block size | `kimi-k31-mc@sha256:5c243ce0…` |
| `gb300_agentx_c1` | 1 | One aggregated TP16 + DCP16 engine across four trays | `kimi-k31-mc@sha256:5c243ce0…` |

- The PD presets select the Dynamo router (Rust frontend) and the distributed Mooncake KV store in host DRAM; Dynamo is built from `3dd0744e`.
- Each runbook covers the services (etcd, NATS, Mooncake master and store sizing), the frontend, and a synthetic-acceptance snippet for throughput measurement. Benchmark-only settings are left out and named.

## Validation

- **Flag by flag against #4907.** The effective configs of all seven points at `f2bb2756` (base recipe deep-merged with each point's override) were compared with the preset commands. The comparison covered every arg and env var of every role. 0 missing and 0 mismatched; the excluded benchmark-only settings are listed in the runbooks.
- **Rendering.** The commands come from a local Python re-implementation (not part of this PR) of the recipes renderer's layering for these presets: layer order, last-wins dedupe, `json_args`, Dynamo parser mapping, the DCP row and the PD pool-mode snap. The official JS renderer was not run locally; this PR's `Recipes` check runs it.
- **Schema.** `recipe.schema.json` (Draft 7): 0 errors.

## Details

- **Hybrid decode.** The schema's `dep` pool renders TP1 ranks, and a role can't set the per-rank TP. So the hybrid decode is a TEP pool on 8 trays whose role args set `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 4` (last wins). That matches the lane's launch: four TP8 engines across two trays each.
- **DEP pools now offered** (`strategy_hardware.multi_node_dep: { gb300: supported }`, `strategy_min_gpus.multi_node_dep: 16`). PD pool modes follow the compatible strategies, so before this the DEP16 preset rendered TP16 pools.
  - **Side effect:** the existing PD decode pool, which the recipe already declares as DEP16, now renders as DEP16 in the baseline (no preset) on the NVIDIA GPUs the pool is sized for, instead of TP16. The vLLM router then gets one `--decode` endpoint per node.
  - Other GPUs keep their TP decode pool (`parallelism: { default: tp, nvidia: dep }`).
  - Aggregated Multi-node DEP shows on GB300 but has not been run on its own; the comment says so.
- **Concurrency 1** is rendered as `vllm serve` (multi-node TP16 + DCP16), because `pd_router` is PD-only. The runbook describes how the lane fronts it with Dynamo.
- The `low_latency_decode` guide text still says TP8 / TP8 + DCP8 without expert parallelism. #66433 edits the same block, so I'll align it after one of them merges. #66433 also adds B300 presets to this file, in a different section.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3] Build the MTP eh_proj low-latency GEMM plan
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On CUDA, `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictorLayer` (the MTP draft layer for `glm_moe_dsa` checkpoints such as GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3) never builds its `eh_proj` low-latency GEMM plan: it checks the draft config's `model_type`, which `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override` rewrites from `glm_moe_dsa` to `deepseek_mtp`. Gate on the target model type instead, as `DeepseekV32MTP` already does. This enables the `eh_proj` rows added in #49791 (SM103), #62843 (SM107) and #64481 (SM100).

## Claims

- Fixes: on SM100, SM103 and SM107 with a BF16 model dtype, the draft's 6144x12288 `eh_proj` now gets the GLM low-latency plan: CuTe skinny GEMM at M 1-4 on SM100/SM107 and M 1-3 on SM103; other M stay on cuBLAS. Before, the plan was never built, so `eh_proj` always ran through `nn.Linear` (cuBLAS).
- Adds a unit test (CPU tensors, mocked configs and submodules) that builds the layer with draft `model_type` `deepseek_mtp` and target `glm_moe_dsa`, and checks that `build_glm52_plan` is called with `eh_proj`'s weight and its plan is kept.

## Validation

Unit tests on main `173d063` (its Python tree over a `2d8e9a9bb7` build's compiled extensions), run on a VR200 (SM107) node:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k "eh_proj or glm"
# with the fix: 5 passed (the new test and 4 existing GLM MTP tests that do not build DeepseekV32MTP)
# test change only, on unpatched main: 1 failed, 4 passed. The new test fails with:
#   AssertionError: Expected 'build_glm52_plan' to be called once. Called 0 times.
```

**Isolated serving A/B: stock vs stock plus only this PR's `mtp.py` change.**
- **Build:** a vLLM `2d8e9a9bb7` build whose `mtp.py` and SM107 table are identical to main `173d063`'s.
- **Config:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4 on 4x VR200 (SM107), lossless MTP K=7 (greedy draft, standard rejection), FP8 KV, `--numa-bind`.
- **Eval:** GSM8K with all 1,319 questions, 8-shot, greedy, at concurrency 4, so the draft's `eh_proj` runs at M <= 4, where the rows apply.

| | stock | + this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `Compiling CuTeDSL kernels: N/N` at startup | 33 | 36 |
| GSM8K accuracy | 90.83% | 91.51% |
| draft acceptance (accepted / draft tokens) | 49.6% | 49.3% |
| mean acceptance length | 4.48 | 4.45 |

- **Acceptance:** within 0.5%.
- **Why +3 compiles, not +4:** the SM107 `eh_proj` row has 4 configs, and its M=2 config equals the TP4 `o_proj` and shared-expert `down_proj` M=2 configs.
- **Reproduce:** serve a `glm_moe_dsa` checkpoint with `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'` and read the startup line.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** as of 2026-11-04, no open PR changes this check. I diffed every open PR updated since 2026-09-15 and ran keyword searches.
- **AI assistance:** This PR is developed with AI assistance, which also ran the tests and measurements above on VR200 nodes. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Named and required tool_choice need a tool parser
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`docs/features/tool_calling.md` says named function calling works "by default", and that `tool_choice="required"` "is enabled by default and will work with any supported model". Since #30613 (first released in v0.14.0), both return HTTP 400 unless the server has loaded a tool parser, and the server loads one only when `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser` are both set. This PR updates the Named and Required Function Calling sections and the `--enable-auto-tool-choice` entry to match. Related: #55754, #55762.

## Claims

- Named and Required Function Calling state that both flags are needed and that a request without a loaded parser returns HTTP 400. They also note that this check does not reject requests to models in the official Mistral format or to gpt-oss models.
- Both sections now point to [Constrained Decoding Behavior](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/docs/features/tool_calling.md#L112-L125) for how far the arguments follow the tool's schema, instead of saying the output strictly matches it. That later section enforces a tool's schema under a structural tag only when the tool sets `strict: true` or the server uses `--tool-strict-level parameter`.
- The `--enable-auto-tool-choice` entry under Automatic Function Calling says that named and required function calling also need it.
- The sentence that alternative decoding backends are on the V1 roadmap is removed; [`docs/usage/v1_guide.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/docs/usage/v1_guide.md#L157) lists them as functional.

## Validation

The behaviour described comes from the code at the base commit `6d01893`:

- [`OnlineRenderer.render_chat()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L263-L290): with no tool parser, and neither a Mistral tokenizer nor gpt-oss, `"auto"` fails with `"auto" tool choice requires --enable-auto-tool-choice and --tool-call-parser to be set`, and `"required"` or a named choice fails with `tool_choice=... requires --tool-call-parser to be set`. Both are 400 `BadRequestError`.
- [`ParserManager.get_tool_parser()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/vllm/parser/parser_manager.py#L33-L35) returns `None` when `enable_auto_tools` is false, so `--tool-call-parser` alone loads no parser. #55754 reproduces this over HTTP with `--tool-call-parser hermes`.
- [`test_tool_choice_validation_without_parser`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py#L2866) covers the case with no parser.

Driving `OnlineRenderer.render_chat()` from the v0.32.0 wheel on CPU, with the Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct tokenizer and no engine, gives the same result. With no tool flags, and with `--tool-call-parser hermes` alone, a request with tools returns 400 for `tool_choice` omitted, `"auto"`, `"required"` and named; with both flags all four are accepted. The check and `get_tool_parser()` are the same in v0.32.0 and at the base commit.

`pre-commit run --files docs/features/tool_calling.md` passes, including `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos`. A local `mkdocs build` did not get past `docs/mkdocs/gen_files/generate_argparse.py`, which imports modules that need the compiled CUDA extensions, so the Read the Docs preview is the render check.

## Details

The 400 is intended. #30613 added it because, without the two flags, these requests "would silently degrade instead of returning a clear error". The docs predate it. Up to v0.11.0 the JSON schema for a named or required call was built in `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` without a parser; #27383 (v0.11.1) moved that into the tool parser.

#55762 proposes loading the configured parser without `--enable-auto-tool-choice` for named and required choices. If it lands, the sentences that name both flags should say that `--tool-call-parser` is enough; that PR does not change the docs. No open PR edits these sections. #60585 adds an Allowed Tools section right after Required Function Calling, next to a line this PR changes, so the second of the two to merge may need a rebase.

This PR leaves out two related points. The error message names only `--tool-call-parser`, but it sits in the validation block that #55762 rewrites. The Responses API does not apply this check (#39221), and the new sentences describe the chat completion API.

This PR was prepared with the help of a coding agent.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Stub owns_indexer and index_epoch in the merged-cache sparse MLA test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_sparse_mla_backend_forward_mqa_fp8_ds_mla_merged_cache` builds its implementation object with`object.__new__(ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl)`, so it has to set by hand every attribute `__init__` would haveset. It sets seven of them but not `owns_indexer` and `index_epoch`. `forward_mqa` has read both since#51309, so the test raises `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute'owns_indexer'` on gfx950.

This adds the two missing assignments, matching what the sibling sparse MLA tests already do.

## Claims

- Test only. No production code changes.
- The values match `__init__`: an owning layer always remaps, so `index_epoch` is never compared and 0 is
  the same starting point `_index_epoch` returns for a fresh buffer.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py` and
  `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sink.py` already stub these two attributes the same way.

## Validation

On gfx950 (MI355X):

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| before | `AttributeError` in 2.0 s |
| after | 1 passed in 4.9 s |

Removing only `owns_indexer` is not enough: the test then fails on `index_epoch` at `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:1250`, where the remap writes the epoch back into the metadata. Both are needed.

## Why CI did not catch it

The test is marked `@requires_gfx950`. The `Attention Kernels` AMD mirror in the main pipeline runs on `device: mi300_1`, which is gfx942, so the test is skipped there. The only step that executes it is `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Attention Kernels Shard %N` in the legacy `test-amd.yaml`, and that pipeline does not gate merges. The test was added this morning by #66532 and the gap showed up in [amd-ci build 15803](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15803/list?jid=01a1c4e8-c43e-4a8e-ad53-8237643d5bc8&tab=output), where it is the single failure in a shard of 3798 passing tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Re-prepare model state after extensible KV cache extension (Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (#56492, on by default with MRV2 on CUDA and ROCm), the first eager decode step after startup kills a Kimi-K3 engine on AMD with `decode_backend=latency_specialized`. This adds a `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache` hook that `extend_kv_cache` calls once it has re-bound the KV views, and Kimi-K3's AMD model state re-runs `prepare_kv()` there.

Found while validating #63486, which disables the extensible KV cache in its Kimi-K3 engine tests until this lands.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode (eager steps) now works with the extensible KV cache. Before this change every TP rank raised `RuntimeError: Kimi-K3 specialized decode: the KV cache was re-bound without prepare_kv`.
- Model states can see the final KV views through a hook that does nothing by default. The safety guard in `SpecializedDecode.plan()` is unchanged.

## Validation

**New test, failing before the fix** (`tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_engine_rebinds_model_state_to_extended_views`, a real Qwen3-0.6B engine, in process). On `main` (5629b26146), with only `raising=False` added, since `main` has no hook to patch:
```
E       AssertionError: assert [] == [(163456, {'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn': (139321971572736, 5356126208), ...})]
```
With the fix it passes: the hook runs exactly once, with the final `num_gpu_blocks` and exactly the views in `runner.kv_caches_by_layer`.

**End to end, 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 8-layer dummy, TP8/DCP8, DSpark k=3.** These use #63486's `tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_e2e_parity.py` with the extensible KV cache on.

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_layer_kernels_match_vllm_layers` (eager) | 1 failed: every rank raises `re-bound without prepare_kv` right after `Extended KV cache to 2460 blocks (14.19 GiB)` | 1 passed (with #63486's NaN-aware `conv_bits`*) |
| `test_verify_steps_replay_the_kernels` (FULL graphs captured before extension) | not reached | 2 passed |

\* Blocks committed during warmup keep their warmup contents. One slot's three unread conv-state entries held NaN in both the kernel's state and the reference, and `torch.equal` treats NaN as unequal. #63486 compares those entries NaN-aware.

Other runs:
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_runtime.py`: 141 passed. This includes `test_plan_refuses_a_kv_cache_bound_behind_its_back`.
- `test_engine_pads_segments_without_a_connector` failed once because another container was holding GPUs 0-3 on the shared host. It passed on an idle GPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`: 51 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all changed files.

CI: the new test runs in `V1 Executor + Worker` (`pytest -v -s v1/worker`, and its AMD mirror). The Kimi-K3 e2e checks need 8x MI355X and run in #63486's Kimi-K3 monokernel steps.

## Details

**Root cause.** With the extensible KV cache, `initialize_kv_cache` binds views that span the whole reservation, and `ModelState.initialize_kv_cache` sees those. After warmup and capture, `extend_kv_cache` commits the measured size. It then rebuilds every view over the same addresses with the final block count (`committed_views`) and re-binds them with `bind_kv_caches`, but it never notifies the model state. `SpecializedDecode.prepare_kv()` records `(data_ptr, numel)` of a KDA state, and `plan()` refuses to run on caches it has not checked. The numel changes, so the first eager step fails. FULL graphs replay without calling `plan()`, which is why only eager steps (and graph-padding fallbacks) hit it.

**Design.** `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache(kv_cache_config)` does nothing by default. `extend_kv_cache` calls it at the end of the `committed is not None` branch, which runs only when views were rebuilt, after binding and the replayssm re-init. `KimiK3ModelState` overrides it to re-run `prepare_kv()`. That call is a TP CPU-group collective. It is safe here because every worker reaches `extend_kv_cache` through the same `collective_rpc`, and whether views get rebuilt depends only on the layout.

Alternatives I rejected:
- Calling `initialize_kv_cache` again. It does one-time setup; for example, DSv4.1's state releases metadata graphs that already-captured FULL graphs use.
- Keying on `data_ptr` alone. That would silently accept a re-bind whose geometry changed, which is exactly what the guard exists to catch.
- Re-preparing lazily in `plan()`. That puts a collective inside the forward pass, including during graph capture.

**Other model states, audited and unchanged.** Kimi-K3 NVIDIA and Muse Spark NVIDIA call `plan()` only at capture, and the addresses do not change. MiniMax-M3 AMD binds capacity views and checks staleness by `data_ptr`. The DSv4/DSv4.1 and Muse Spark AMD mono runtimes read pointers and strides on every launch. hisparse and replayssm are already re-bound in `extend_kv_cache`.

**Supersedes #66357.** #66357 makes the same runtime change (the no-op `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache` hook, the call from `extend_kv_cache`, and the Kimi-K3 AMD override). This PR also factors out `_prepare_kv()`, updates the related docstrings and the `plan()` error text, and tests through a real engine, so #66357 is closed in favour of this one.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Add prefill_context_kv_only for P/D prefill instances
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On a P/D prefill instance, a DFlash-based drafter (DFlash, DSpark, DFlash2, XPress, ...) only needs to store the context K/V that the decode instance reads. This PR adds `prefill_context_kv_only` to the speculative config. Set on the prefill instance, it makes the drafter schedule no drafts, reserve no lookahead KV slots, capture no draft CUDA graphs and, for draft models that name their context K/V modules, free the draft weights that only drafting reads. Requests that decode on that instance run without speculation. It follows #62784 (per-step K=0) and takes its lookahead and speculator-flag handling from #56957.

The option is set explicitly because `kv_role` does not identify a prefill instance: one that also loads from or offloads to a KV store through `MultiConnector` has the `kv_both` role.

Related: #62923 does the same for Qwen3 DSpark, behind an opt-in flag with a separate model class. #56957 adds a DSpark prefill-only mode for PP > 1 with non-NIXL connectors and the DeepSeek-V4 draft. This PR keeps `num_speculative_tokens` unchanged, because it also sizes state the decode instance loads (e.g. the Mamba state).

Since this PR takes similar approaches, the authors of #56957 (@lucifer1004) and #62923 (@LLLZeSheng) are added as co-authors, as is @njhill, whose simplification of the weight-freeing opt-in is squashed in.

## Design

- `SpeculatorConfig.supports_prefill_context_kv_only` declares support: `DFlashSpeculatorConfig` and its subclasses; other speculators reject the option. It needs a `kv_transfer_config` that produces KV (`kv_producer` or `kv_both`), and it turns off adaptive verification and dynamic speculative decoding.
- `SpeculatorConfig.num_scheduled_spec_tokens` is the number of spec tokens scheduled per step: `num_speculative_tokens`, or 0 with the option. The scheduler's `num_spec_tokens` and every warmup batch read it, so the prefill instance schedules no drafts, doesn't pad a one-token request (a full prefix-cache hit) to 1 + K rows, and reserves no blocks for drafts. `DFlashSpeculatorConfig.num_lookahead_tokens` follows it. Without the option it equals `num_speculative_tokens`, so nothing else changes.
- Weight freeing: a draft model whose class has `context_kv_modules()`, the modules its context K/V path reads, frees the rest; subclasses inherit it. `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` defines it, so DFlash, Qwen3 DSpark, DFlash2, XPress, LiLiCorr and Ripple DFlash2 use its list; Gemma4, MiniMax-M3 and Muse Spark DSpark have their own. Other draft models keep every weight.
- The model runner skips the drafter's EPLB registration (its MoE layers never run), then calls `DraftModelSpeculator.free_unused_weights()` after `load_model`. `DFlashSpeculator` keeps the modules the draft model names and the weights shared with the target.
- Draft weight updates are refused: `supports_draft_weight_updates()` is False, and starting one raises an error.

## Validation

1P1D on one GB300 node, `main` (`03ce803be9`) and this PR side by side, with the option set on the PR's prefill instance only, 24 greedy chat requests:

| Pair | Prefill weights | Prefill KV cache | Prefill CUDA graphs | Decode outputs | Decode drafts / accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (k=16) | 17.3 → 15.5 GiB | 1,304,064 → 1,366,016 tokens (+4.8%) | 5.73 → 2.57 GiB | 24/24 identical | 1,391 / 3,374 in both |
| 8B pair, `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + CPU `OffloadingConnector` with `kv_both`) on both instances | 17.3 → 15.5 GiB | 1,304,064 → 1,366,016 tokens (+4.8%) | 5.73 → 2.57 GiB | 24/24 identical | 1,391 / 3,374 in both |

The prefill instances proposed no drafts in either stack. A prefill instance with DP=2 and an idle rank gives the same 24 outputs, and requests sent straight to it decode without speculation.

The hybrid 27B pair (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark`, k=8) no longer starts over NIXL on current `main`, with or without this PR: every instance fails `KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions` on the target's attention layers, also with `--block-size 128`. At the previous revision of this PR, on `main` `7ecc83a987`, it gave 24/24 identical decode outputs with 1,200 / 3,349 drafts / accepted in both stacks; prefill weights 55.3 → 52.0 GiB, KV cache 469,233 → 509,990 tokens (+8.7%), CUDA graphs 10.24 → 4.04 GiB.

Weight freeing per draft model (dummy weights, public configs): the context K/V written before and after freeing is byte-identical for Qwen3 DFlash (1.80 GiB freed), DSpark (3.31), DFlash2 (3.34), XPress (1.95), Ripple DFlash2 (7.28), Gemma4 DSpark (2.50), MiniMax-M3 DSpark (1.79, fused and unfused paths) and Muse Spark DSpark (9.25). With the base list instead of their overrides, Gemma4, MiniMax-M3 and Muse Spark fail; so does the base list without `fc`. The GPU test covers the base list and Gemma4's.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_context_kv_modules.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
```

| File | This PR | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `test_dflash_lookahead.py` | 6 passed | 6 failed (no `prefill_context_kv_only`) |
| `test_context_kv_modules.py` | 2 passed | 2 failed |
| `test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` | 38 passed | 38 passed |
| `test_scheduler.py` | 291 passed, 3 failed | 291 passed, 3 failed |

The 3 `test_scheduler.py` failures are pipeline-parallel tests that need more than the one GPU these runs had; they fail the same way on `main`. The new padding and KV-role tests fail without their fixes (`assert 4 == 1`; `DID NOT RAISE ValueError`).

No CI step covers P/D with speculative decoding (that step is disabled), hence the runs above.

## Purpose

#47035 skipped the `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` parametrization of `test_transcription_validation_whisper.py` because #46780 had limited that backend to bf16, and Whisper runs in fp16. 
With the current AITER version (v0.1.29), `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend.supported_dtypes` includes `torch.float16`, so the skip is no longer needed.

This restores the behaviour from before #47035: the parametrization runs again with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1` (`_AITER_ENV`, which has been defined but unused since the skip was added).

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), main at 3a104103ac with AITER v0.1.29 (`rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-c67ca115e7d64f7d`, vLLM built from source), `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` as in the AMD Speech to Text step:

- `pytest -v -s entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation_whisper.py`
- `pytest -v -s entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation_whisper.py -k ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`
- `pytest -v -s entrypoints/speech_to_text`

- The server log shows `Using ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN backend`, `dtype=torch.float16`, and the AITER fp16 kernels being loaded.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Register the cudnn backend for FlashInfer BF16 mm
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Only the cute-dsl backend is wired up for unquantized BF16 linear layers, and it is restricted to sm_10x. That restriction is correct for cute-dsl (FlashInfer raises `BackendSupportedError` for it on sm_120), but `mm_bf16` also has a cudnn backend that runs there, so consumer Blackwell (sm_120/121) currently has no FlashInfer path for unquantized BF16 at all.

## Changes

Splits the shape/layout checks out of the cute-dsl predicate into a shared `_bf16_mm_shape_supported`, keeps the sm_10x gate on cute-dsl alone, and registers a new `flashinfer_cudnn` entry in `_FLASHINFER_BF16_BACKENDS`. The cudnn path is bounded by output width (`N <= 128`): swept on GB10 (sm_121, K=5120), FlashInfer wins 5-6x at `N<=128` and loses 2-4x at `N=512`, so diverting every unquantized GEMM would be a net loss on a model with a mix of widths.

```
        M=1    M=2    M=4    M=8   M=16   M=32
  N=96  1.09   6.14   6.15   1.26   1.28   1.20
 N=128  1.01   5.38   1.26   1.35   1.42   1.51
 N=192  0.85   4.31   1.17   1.26   1.38   1.31
 N=256  1.14   1.38   1.26   1.37   0.89   0.96
 N=512  0.27   0.37   0.41   0.53   0.63   0.75
```
(cuBLAS_us / flashinfer_us, >1 means FlashInfer wins)

Selection is unchanged by default; this only makes `--linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` usable for BF16, which was already an accepted `LinearBackend` value for NVFP4.

## Relationship to other open work

This generalizes the win a GDN-specific custom op (routing `in_proj_ba` to FlashInfer, #57318) was chasing for one projection. `in_proj_ba`'s output width (`2 * num_v_heads`) is `<= 96` for every shipped Qwen GDN model, so it qualifies for this path automatically via `--linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` (or `--unquantized-linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` from #59021) — no GDN-specific routing code needed. Once this lands, #57318's bespoke custom op can likely be simplified or dropped in favor of this general path.

## Test plan

- `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py').read())"` — parses cleanly.
- Selection unchanged by default (`linear_backend` unset continues to resolve to `default_unquantized_gemm`); the new `flashinfer_cudnn` entry is only reachable when explicitly requested.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and this description.
